how: Stand with your back flat on the wall, feet a short step out and hip-width apart.
Slide down the wall until your knees are a little bent, a quarter of the way to sitting.
Shift your feet so your knees sit right above your ankles, then hold still.
Breathe slowly and evenly, counting out loud so you never hold your breath.
The clock times the hold, and when it ends, slide back up the wall to stand.
208.name: Weighted wall sit
208.setup: The vest snug, back flat on the wall.
208.stop: Stop when you slide or your knees ache.
tips: Keep your head, shoulders and the back of the vest against the wall the whole time.
Let your arms hang loose and relax your hands and jaw.
Push your whole foot into the floor, heels too, to feel the front of your thighs work.

209.cue: Climb steadily, walk down carefully. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Check the stairs are clear and well lit, then stand at the bottom beside the handrail.
Rest one hand lightly on the rail and lean your chest a little forward.
Climb at a steady beat, one foot on each step, placing your whole foot every time.
At the top, turn and walk down slowly with a hand on the rail, then climb again.
Keep a hard pace, too fast to talk on the way up.
209.name: Weighted stair climb
209.setup: The vest snug, a handrail within reach.
tips: Push through the whole foot on the step above rather than springing off your toes.
Keep your eyes a few steps ahead, not on your feet.
Slide your hand along the rail as you go so it is always there to grab.

21.cue: Drop the back knee, front shin upright. Count out loud, breathe out as you rise.
21.hint: Lower the back foot or shorten your stance if your back thigh feels tight.
how: Stand with your back to a bed or sofa and rest the top of one foot on its edge.
Set the front foot far enough forward that its shin stays upright at the bottom.
Lower the back knee towards the floor, leaning your chest slightly forward.
Breathe out and push through the front foot to rise back to the top.
Count each rise out loud; finish one leg, press Switch sides, then do the other.
21.name: Bulgarian split squat
21.setup: Rear foot on the edge of a bed or sofa behind you.
21.stop: Stop when you wobble or your knee caves in. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep most of your weight on the front foot and let the back leg only balance you.
Lay the laces of the back foot flat on the edge so it rests rather than pushes.
Keep your front knee in line with your middle toes all the way down and up.

210.cue: Sit down between your heels, chest up, stand. Breathe out as you stand.
how: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips, toes turned out a little.
Hold the ball against your chest with both hands underneath it, elbows pointing down.
Sit straight down between your heels until your hips reach knee height.
Stand back up from the bottom, breathing out as you rise.
One rep is down and back to standing tall, so count as you reach the top.
210.name: Ball squat
210.setup: The ball held at your chest.
210.stop: Stop when your back rounds or your knees cave in.
tips: Keep the ball tight to your chest so it does not pull you forward.
Let your elbows travel down inside your knees at the bottom to guide your knees out.
Press your heels down and stand up by pushing the floor away.

211.cue: Ball overhead, arms straight, ribs down, walk steadily. Breathe evenly.
how: Clear the hallway floor and pick a turning point at each end before you start.
Press the ball straight up above your head with both hands, arms fully straight.
Stand tall with your ribs pulled down so your back stays flat under the ball.
Walk at a steady, normal pace and turn with small steps at each end.
Breathe evenly and keep walking until the clock ends.
211.name: Overhead carry
211.setup: A light ball, a clear hallway.
211.stop: Stop when your back arches or your arms drop.
tips: Squeeze the ball between your palms and push it up toward the ceiling.
Keep your upper arms close by your ears rather than drifting forward.
Take short, smooth steps so the ball stays still above your head.

212.cue: Ball high on one side, chop it low to the other. Count out loud, breathe out on the chop.
how: Stand with your feet wider than your hips, knees soft, the ball in both hands.
Lift the ball high above one shoulder with long arms, turning your chest toward it.
Chop it fast across your body to outside the other knee, bending your knees as you go.
Breathe out hard on the chop, then breathe in as you lift it back up more slowly.
One rep is high to low and back up: all reps on one side, then press Switch sides.
212.name: Ball chop
212.stop: Stop when your hips swing with your arms. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep your hips and knees facing forward and let your chest do the turning.
Tighten your belly before each chop so you stop the ball where you choose.
Follow the ball with your eyes so your head turns with your chest.

213.cue: Lift it overhead, slam it down, hinge to pick up. Count out loud, breathe out on the slam.
how: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, the floor just in front of your feet clear.
Bend your hips and knees and pick the ball up with both hands, back flat.
Lift it overhead fast, rising up onto your toes as your arms go long.
Slam it hard onto the floor just ahead of your feet, bending hips and knees as it drops.
Breathe out hard on the slam, and count one rep each time the ball hits the floor.
213.name: Ball slam
213.setup: A slam ball on a sturdy floor, never a bouncing ball.
213.stop: Stop when your back rounds on the pick-up.
tips: Pull the ball down with your belly and back, not just your arms.
Look at one spot on the floor just ahead of your toes and aim every slam there.
Keep a steady rhythm, taking a quick breath in as you lift before each slam.

214.cue: Throw from your chest at the wall, catch softly. Count out loud, breathe out on the throw.
how: Stand about two big steps from the wall, feet hip-width apart and knees a little bent.
Hold the ball at your chest, hands on its sides, thumbs behind and elbows down.
Push it hard and straight at the wall at chest height until your arms are straight.
Catch it with soft arms and let your elbows bend to bring it back to your chest.
Breathe out on each throw, and count one rep each time you catch the ball.
214.name: Ball chest pass
214.setup: A solid wall and a ball that bounces back.
214.stop: Stop when your throws get sloppy.
tips: Aim for one spot on the wall so every throw comes straight back to your hands.
Keep your elbows down and close at the start so the push comes from your chest.
Shift your weight onto the balls of your feet as you throw to add snap.

215.cue: Roll slowly along your calves, then the front of your thighs. Breathe slowly.
how: Sit on the floor with the roller under your calves and your hands behind you.
Lift your hips and roll slowly from just above your ankles to just below your knees.
Turn onto your front and rest on your forearms with the roller under your thighs.
Roll slowly from just above your knees to the top of your thighs and back.
Take about 2 to 3 s each way, breathe slowly, and keep an easy pace for the time shown.
215.name: Roll calves and thighs
tips: Hold your body in one straight line from shoulders to knees as you roll the thighs.
Turn your toes in or out a little to roll the inner and outer sides.
Pause for a slow breath on a tight spot instead of rolling fast over it.

216.cue: Roll slowly along your seat, then the side of your back. Breathe slowly.
how: Sit on the roller with your knees bent, feet flat and hands on the floor behind you.
Roll slowly back and forth over your seat, about 2 s each way.
Turn onto your side with the roller under the side of your back, bottom arm long overhead.
Roll slowly from your lower ribs up to just below your armpit and back.
Breathe slowly and move at an easy pace for the time shown.
216.name: Roll hips and back
tips: Lean onto one hip, then the other, to reach each side of your seat.
Keep the bottom arm reaching long overhead to open the side of your back.
Keep your belly firm on your side so your body rolls as one piece.

217.cue: Lower one arm and the other leg, stay balanced. Count out loud, breathe out as you lower.
how: Sit at one end of the roller and lie back so your head and hips both rest on it.
Bend your knees, feet flat and hip-width apart, and reach both arms straight up.
Lower one arm overhead and straighten the other leg over the floor.
Breathe out as you lower, then bring both back and switch sides.
Count one rep each time an arm and the other leg go down and come back.
217.name: Roller dead bug
217.setup: Lie on the roller along your spine, feet on the floor.
217.stop: Stop when you roll off or your back arches. Alternate sides; each lower counts one.
tips: Press your lower back gently into the roller the whole time so your ribs stay down.
Press the planted foot into the floor to hold you steady on the roller.
Keep the straight leg hovering off the floor, never resting it down.

218.cue: Sit back, chest up, stand. Count out loud, breathe out as you stand.
how: Pull both straps tight so the pack sits high and close on your back.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out a little, chest up.
Sit back and down until your thighs pass level, arms reaching forward.
Drive up from the bottom, breathing out as you stand.
One rep is down and back up to standing tall, so count as you reach the top.
218.name: Backpack squat
218.setup: A backpack of 8-12 kg on your back, straps tight.
218.stop: Stop when your heels lift or your knees cave in.
tips: Keep your back flat and chest up so the pack never pulls your shoulders round.
Reach your arms forward as you sit down to balance the pack on your back.
Load it to 8-12 kg: 1-L water bottles weigh 1 kg each, a hardback about 1 kg.

219.cue: Hips back, back flat, lift it, stand tall. Count out loud, breathe out as you stand.
how: Any weight you can grip: a bag of books or bottles, a full jug, a kettlebell or dumbbells.
Nothing near? Lift a light chair without wheels by the sides of its seat.
Stand close to it, feet hip-width, push your hips back and grip it with a flat back.
Stand up tall, breathing out, then push your hips back to lower it.
One rep is from below your knees up to standing tall, so count at the top.

dumbbells: Set the dumbbells on the floor just outside your feet, handles in line with your ankles.
Stand between them, feet hip-width, push your hips back and grip both, back flat.
Stand up tall, breathing out, then push your hips back to lower them.
One rep is from below your knees up to standing tall, so count at the top.
kettlebell: Set the kettlebell on the floor between your feet, its handle in line with your ankles.
Stand close to it, feet hip-width, push your hips back and grip the handle, back flat.
Stand up tall, breathing out, then push your hips back to lower it.
One rep is from below your knees up to standing tall, so count at the top.

219.name: Deadlift with a weight
219.setup: A weight of 10-20 kg on the floor in front of you: a bag, a jug, a kettlebell.

setups.dumbbells: Two dumbbells, 10-20 kg together, on the floor in front of you.
setups.kettlebell: A kettlebell of 10-20 kg on the floor in front of you.

tips: Pick a weight where 10 reps are work and 20 hard: the game says when to go heavier.
1 L of water weighs 1 kg, a hardback about 1 kg: most people start at 10-20 kg.
Keep the weight close so it brushes your legs all the way down and up.

22.cue: Lower for 3 seconds, rise in 1. Count out loud, breathe out as you rise.
how: Stand side-on to the desk with one hand on its edge and feet about a metre apart.
Keep your feet hip-width apart, the back heel up and your body tall between them.
Lower the back knee for a slow count of three until it hovers just above the floor.
Breathe out and rise in one count by pushing through the front foot.
Count each rise out loud; finish one leg, press Switch sides, then do the other.
22.name: Split squat, 3-s lowering
22.setup: One hand on the desk edge, feet a long step apart.
22.stop: Stop when you lose the 3-s lowering. Count the weaker side.
tips: Count the three seconds out loud so the last part of the lowering stays slow.
Keep breathing in as you lower, never hold your breath to stay steady.
Use the desk for balance only, so your legs control the speed.

221.cue: Lower toward one hand, the other arm straight, alternate. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Push the keyboard back and grip the desk edge with your hands twice shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet back until your body is one straight line from heels to head.
Bend one elbow to lower your chest toward that hand, the other arm staying straight.
Push back up, breathing out, then lower toward the other hand.
Alternate sides every rep; a push-up to one side and then the other counts one.
221.name: Desk archer push-up
221.setup: Hands wide on a sturdy desk edge, keyboard pushed back, feet back.
221.stop: Stop when your hips twist or sag. A push-up to each side counts one.
tips: Keep the straight arm long and light: it steadies you while the bent arm works.
Turn the working hand's fingers slightly out so the elbow tracks over the wrist.
Keep your hips square to the desk so the effort stays in your chest and arm.

222.cue: Lower on one arm in 3 s, push up with both. Count out loud, breathe out as you push.
how: Place one hand on the desk edge in line with the middle of your chest.
Step your feet back and wide, body straight from heels to head, free hand on your hip.
Lower your chest toward the desk on the one arm, counting three slow beats.
At the bottom, set the free hand down and push up with both, breathing out.
Each slow lowering counts one rep; do one side, press Switch sides, then the other.
222.name: One-arm desk lowering
222.setup: One hand on a sturdy desk edge under your chest, feet wide behind.
222.stop: Stop when your hips twist or you drop fast. Count the weaker side.
tips: Spread your feet wider than your hips: a wide base stops your body twisting.
Squeeze your seat and belly so your hips stay level with your shoulders.
Keep the working elbow close to your side, not flared out.

223.cue: Lower and push up on one arm, body straight. Count out loud, breathe out as you push.
how: Place one hand on the desk edge in line with the middle of your chest.
Walk your feet back and wide until your body is one straight line, free hand on your back.
Lower your chest toward the desk edge, elbow close to your side.
Push the desk away until the arm is straight, breathing out as you push.
Each lower and push counts one rep; do one side, press Switch sides, then the other.
223.name: One-arm desk push-up
223.setup: One hand on a sturdy desk edge under your chest, feet wide behind.
223.stop: Stop when your hips twist or sag. Count the weaker side.
tips: Brace your belly and squeeze your seat so your body moves as one piece.
Turn your hips slightly toward the working arm if they twist away.
Press the whole palm into the desk, fingers spread, for a firm base.

224.cue: Three seconds down, pause, push up on one arm. Count out loud, breathe out as you push.
how: Place one hand on the desk edge in line with the middle of your chest.
Walk your feet back, closer together than for the one-arm push-up, body straight.
Lower toward the desk over three slow beats, then pause for one beat.
Push back up in 1 s, breathing out as you push, never holding your breath.
Each slow rep counts as one; do one side, press Switch sides, then the other.
224.name: Slow one-arm desk push-up
224.setup: One hand on a sturdy desk edge under your chest, feet close.
224.stop: Stop when your hips twist or you hold your breath. Count the weaker side.
tips: Narrow feet make it harder to stay square: keep them together only while hips stay level.
Say the beats out loud so the lowering never speeds up.
Keep the free hand on your back or hip, never on the desk.

225.cue: Pull your chest to the frame on one arm. Count out loud, breathe out as you pull.
how: Face the frame's edge on the side without hinges and wrap one hand around it.
Set your toes a hand's length from the base and lean back until the arm is straight.
Pull your chest to the frame, elbow close to your side, then lower slowly.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lean back.
Each pull counts as one rep; do one side, press Switch sides, then the other.
225.name: One-arm doorframe row
225.setup: One hand on a solid doorframe edge at chest height, toes a hand's length from its base.
225.stop: Stop when your hand slips or your hips twist. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep the free hand hovering by the frame, ready to catch you.
Start each pull by drawing the shoulder blade back, then bend the arm.
Grip only where your whole hand closes around the frame, never trim with fingertips.

227.cue: Lean back far on one arm, pull, lower in 3 s. Count out loud, breathe out as you pull.
how: Face the frame's edge on the side without hinges and wrap one hand around it.
Put your toes against the base and lean back until the arm is straight.
Pull your chest to the frame in 1 s, then lower over three slow beats.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.
Each pull counts as one rep. Do every rep on one side, then press Switch sides.
227.name: Steep one-arm doorframe row
227.setup: One hand around a solid doorframe edge, toes against its base.
227.stop: Stop when your hand creeps down the frame or your hips twist. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep your toes against the base every set; when your hand creeps, the set is done.
Keep your body straight from heels to head, hips in line.
Rest the free hand on your belly, ready to grab the frame if your grip slips.

228.cue: Lean back on the towel, pull your chest to the door. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Tie one big knot at one end of a bath towel.
Push the door open, lay the towel over its top: knot on the far side, the rest on yours.
Shut the door till it clicks, lock it, then pull the towel hard: the door must not move.
Grip the two bottom corners, toes at the door, lean back on straight arms, body straight.
Pull your chest to the door, breathing out, lower slowly. Each pull is one rep.
228.name: Towel door row
228.setup: A knotted bath towel over the top of a solid door that you push to open.
228.stop: Stop when the door moves or your hips sag.
tips: The right door opens away from you: you push it open and its hinges are on the far side.
A thinner towel lets the door shut all the way. Use one with no holes or thin spots.
No lock? Ask the others at home not to open that door while you train.

229.cue: Pull your chest up to the towel and hold, elbows back. Count out loud, keep breathing.
how: Lay the towel over the door's top, its end knot on the far side; shut and lock the door.
Pull the towel hard once: the door must not move.
Grip the two bottom corners, toes against the door, and lean back on straight arms.
Pull your chest up to your hands and hold there, elbows back and shoulders down.
Keep breathing slowly; the clock runs while your chest stays up.
229.name: Towel door row hold
229.setup: A knotted bath towel over the top of a solid door that you push to open.
229.stop: Stop when the door moves or your shoulders shrug.
tips: Set your toes against the door before the clock starts, so every hold is the same lean.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together as if holding a pencil between them.
Keep your hips up so your body stays one straight line.

23.cue: Sit all the way down on one leg, other leg forward. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Face the desk a small step back, fingertips resting on its edge, arms reaching forward.
Stand on one leg and hold the other leg straight out in front, heel off the floor.
Sit back and down on the standing leg until your thigh rests on your calf.
Breathe out and stand back up, the fingertips only steadying you, never pulling.
Count each rise out loud; finish one leg, press Switch sides, then do the other.
23.name: Assisted pistol
23.setup: Fingertips on the desk edge; the desk must not move.
23.stop: Stop when your knee caves in or you need more than fingertips. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep the standing heel flat and that knee tracking over your middle toes.
Lean your chest forward as you sit to keep your weight over the standing foot.
Go all the way down every time; a rise from halfway does not count.

230.cue: Arms straight, squeeze your shoulder blades back, release. Count out loud, breathe out.
how: Lay the towel over the door's top, its end knot on the far side; shut and lock the door.
Pull the towel hard once: the door must not move.
Grip the two bottom corners, toes against the door, and lean back far on straight arms.
Arms straight, squeeze your shoulder blades back and down, breathing out; hold a beat.
Let your shoulders slide forward again. Each squeeze counts as one rep.
230.name: Towel door shoulder-blade pull
230.setup: A knotted bath towel over the top of a solid door you push to open, your toes against it.
230.stop: Stop when your elbows bend or your shoulders shrug.
tips: Think of putting your shoulder blades in your back pockets.
Never bend the elbows: the move is all in the shoulder blades.
Keep your toes against the door each set so the lean stays the same.

231.cue: Pull up with both, lower on one arm in 3 s. Count out loud, breathe out as you pull.
how: Lay the towel over the door's top, its end knot on the far side; shut and lock the door.
Pull the towel hard once: the door must not move.
Toes against the door, lean back far and pull your chest up with both arms, breathing out.
Let go with one hand and lower over three slow beats on the other arm.
Each slow lowering counts one rep; do one side, press Switch sides, then the other.
231.name: One-arm towel door lowering
231.setup: A knotted bath towel over the top of a solid door you push to open, your toes against it.
231.stop: Stop when you drop fast or the door moves. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep the free hand near the towel, ready to grab it again.
Fight for the slow count: the lowering is the strong part.
Keep your body straight; a sag means it is time to rest.

232.cue: Lean back on one arm, pull your chest to the towel. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Lay the towel over the door's top, its end knot on the far side; shut and lock the door.
Pull the towel hard once: the door must not move.
Hold the towel's free end, toes against the door, and lean back on the straight arm.
Pull your chest up to your hand, breathing out, then lower with control.
Keep your hips square; do every rep on one side, then press Switch sides.
232.name: One-arm towel door row
232.setup: A knotted bath towel over the top of a solid door that you push to open.
232.stop: Stop when your hips twist or the door moves. Count the weaker side.
tips: Spread your feet a little wider than your hips to stop the twist.
Start each pull with the shoulder blade, then bend the elbow.
Keep your toes against the door each time so your record stays fair.

234.cue: Push through your heel, hips up, lower slowly. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Lie on your back on the bed or sofa, knees bent and heels near your seat.
Straighten one leg in line with the other thigh, arms flat at your sides.
Push through the heel of the bent leg and lift your hips until body and thigh line up.
Hold a beat at the top, then lower slowly, breathing out as you lift.
Each lift counts as one rep; do one side, press Switch sides, then the other.
234.name: Single-leg bridge on the bed
234.setup: Lie on a bed or sofa, one foot flat, the other leg straight.
234.stop: Stop when your lower back arches or your hips drop. Count the weaker side.
tips: Press the heel down hard: a soft mattress makes your hips work to stay level.
Keep both hips at the same height as you rise.
Squeeze your seat at the top rather than arching your back.

235.cue: Walk your heels out in small steps, then back. Count out loud, breathe steadily.
how: Lie on your back on the bed or sofa, knees bent, heels near your seat.
Lift your hips into a bridge, arms flat at your sides.
Walk your heels away in small steps until your legs are almost straight, hips up.
Walk them back in, keeping the hips up, and breathe steadily throughout.
Each walk out and back counts as one rep.
235.name: Hamstring walkout on the bed
235.setup: Lie on a bed or sofa, heels down, hips lifted.
235.stop: Stop when your hips drop or the backs of your thighs cramp.
tips: Take small steps: the further out you go, the harder the hold.
Keep your hips lifted the whole set and lower them only at the end.
Dig your heels into the mattress to feel the backs of your thighs.

236.cue: Lift one foot and hold. Count out loud, keep breathing.
how: Rest your forearms on the desk edge, elbows under your shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your body is one straight line from heels to head.
Lift one foot a hand's width off the floor and hold, hips level.
Count out loud; when this side ends, press Switch sides and lift the other foot.
236.name: Desk plank, one foot up
236.setup: Forearms on a sturdy desk edge, feet back, body straight.
236.stop: Stop when your hips sag or twist. Count the weaker side.
tips: Squeeze your seat and belly as if bracing for a light poke.
Keep your hips level when the foot lifts, with no twist to one side.
Push the desk away with your forearms so your upper back stays firm.

237.cue: Draw one knee to your chest and hold. Count out loud, keep breathing.
how: Place your hands on the desk edge under your shoulders, arms straight.
Walk your feet back until your body is one straight line from heels to head.
Draw one knee toward your chest and hold it there, the other leg straight.
Count out loud; when this side ends, press Switch sides and draw in the other knee.
237.name: Desk tuck plank
237.setup: Hands on a sturdy desk edge, feet back, body straight.
237.stop: Stop when your hips sag or your back rounds. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep the straight leg's heel pressing back so the line stays long.
Pull the knee in with your belly, not by rounding your back.
Keep your shoulders over your hands the whole time.

238.cue: Hips up, body straight sideways, hold. Count out loud, keep breathing.
how: Stand side-on to the desk and rest one forearm on its edge, elbow under the shoulder.
Step your feet out to the side until your body leans in one straight line, feet stacked.
Lift your hips so heels, hips and head line up, and hold.
Breathe slowly; hold as long as you can, press Switch sides, then hold the other side.
238.name: Desk side plank
238.setup: One forearm on a sturdy desk edge, side-on, feet stacked behind.
238.stop: Stop when your hips drop or your shoulder shrugs. Count the weaker side.
tips: Push the desk away with your forearm so the shoulder stays strong.
Keep your top hip stacked over the bottom one, not rolling forward.
Look straight ahead so your neck stays in line.

239.cue: Hips up, lift the top leg and hold. Count out loud, keep breathing.
how: Rest one forearm on the desk edge, side-on, elbow under the shoulder.
Step your feet out to the side until your body is one straight line, feet stacked.
Lift your hips, then raise the top leg a hand's width and hold.
Breathe slowly; hold as long as you can, press Switch sides, then hold the other side.
239.name: Desk side plank, leg up
239.setup: One forearm on a sturdy desk edge, side-on, feet stacked behind.
239.stop: Stop when your hips drop or twist. Count the weaker side.
tips: Lift the top leg straight up, not forward, toes pointing ahead.
Press the bottom foot's edge into the floor to stay steady.
Keep both hips stacked as the leg rises.

24.cue: One leg forward, sit all the way down, stand. Count out loud, breathe out as you rise.
how: Stand in clear space with the desk just within reach at your side to catch yourself.
Stand on one leg, reach both arms forward and lift the other leg straight out in front.
Sit down on the standing leg all the way to the bottom, heel flat.
Breathe out and stand straight back up, keeping the free leg off the floor.
Count each rise out loud; finish one leg, press Switch sides, then do the other.
24.name: Pistol squat
24.setup: Clear space; the desk within reach to catch yourself.
24.stop: Stop when your heel lifts or your knee caves in. Count the weaker side.
tips: Reach your arms further forward as you sink to keep your balance over the foot.
Pull the toes of the free leg up towards you to keep that leg straight and high.
Stay tight at the bottom and drive straight up, with no bounce.

241.cue: Squat, stand and reach both arms up, keep the pace. Breathe out as you reach.
how: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart in the cleared space.
Sit your hips back into a squat, hands reaching forward.
Stand up quickly and reach both arms overhead, rising onto your toes.
Go straight back into the next squat, breathing out as you reach.
Keep a hard pace, too fast to talk.
241.name: Squat to reach
241.setup: Clear a small space with room overhead.
tips: Keep your heels down in the squat and rise onto your toes only at the top.
Reach long through your fingertips to open your chest each time.
Keep your knees in line with your toes as you go down.

242.cue: Two quick punches, then duck into a half squat. Breathe out on every punch.
how: Stand in a boxing stance, one foot ahead, fists by your chin.
Throw two quick punches straight ahead, pulling each fist back to the chin.
Duck down into a half squat, chest up, then rise straight back up.
Breathe out sharply on every punch and keep the rhythm going.
Keep a hard pace where you can say only a word or two.
242.name: Punch and duck
242.setup: Clear a small space, fists up by your chin.
tips: Turn your hips and back foot into each punch for speed.
Never lock the elbow: stop each punch just short of straight.
Keep your eyes forward as you duck, back straight.

243.cue: Each knee drive to the wall counts one, so a left and a right make two. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Put your hands on the wall at shoulder height, arms straight.
Walk your feet back until your body leans in one straight line.
Drive one knee up toward the wall, then switch legs quickly.
Each knee drive counts one, so a left and a right make two.
Keep switching at a fast pace, breathing in rhythm with your knees.
243.name: Wall climbers
243.setup: Hands on a wall at shoulder height, feet back, body straight.
tips: Keep your hips low and level as the knees drive.
Push the wall away so your shoulders stay strong.
Land each foot softly on the ball to keep it quiet.

244.cue: Step back, step in, stand and reach, no jumping. Breathe out as you stand.
how: Stand facing the desk, a step back from its edge.
Put your hands on the desk edge and step one foot back, then the other, into a plank.
Step the feet back in one at a time, then stand tall and reach both arms overhead.
Breathe out as you stand and reach, and keep moving without a break.
Keep a hard pace where you can say only a word or two.
244.name: Desk step-back burpee
244.setup: Hands on a sturdy desk edge, room behind you to step back.
tips: Keep your body straight in the plank at the desk, hips in line.
Step, never jump, so it stays quiet.
Lock your hands on the edge before each step back.

245.cue: Heel to your buttock, knees side by side, stand tall. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk with the near hand on it and your feet together.
Bend the outside knee and hold that ankle or foot with the hand on the same side.
Draw the heel to your buttock, knees side by side, and stand tall.
Tuck your tailbone a little and breathe slowly into the front of the thigh.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
245.name: Standing quad stretch
245.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, a hand on it.
245.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if your knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Keep the bent knee pointing at the floor, not out to the side.
Loop a towel round the ankle if your hand cannot reach it.
Squeeze your seat to feel more stretch without pulling harder.

246.cue: Front knee over ankle, back knee straight, arms up. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand tall beside the desk, then step one foot back a long stride onto its toes.
Bend the front knee over the ankle and lower until that thigh is close to level.
Straighten the back knee and press the back heel away from you.
Reach both arms up beside your ears, hands off the knee, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
246.name: High lunge
246.setup: A long stride of clear floor beside the desk.
246.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if your front knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Keep your hips square to the front, the back hip drawn forward.
Rest your fingertips on the desk if you wobble, then lift them again.
Tuck your tailbone a little to feel the stretch at the front of the back hip.

247.cue: Hips square, back flat, fold over the front leg. Breathe slowly.
how: Step one foot back a leg-length, back toes turned out a little, hips facing forward.
Straighten both knees and hinge forward from the hips with a long, flat back.
Lower your fingertips to the floor or the books beside the front foot.
Breathe slowly, then rise slowly with a flat back at the end of the hold.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
247.name: Pyramid
247.setup: Clear floor, feet a leg-length apart, two books by your front foot.
247.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or a tug high under the buttock; never bounce.
tips: Draw the front hip back so both hips face the front.
Keep your hands on the books if the floor is too far, both knees straight.
Lead with your chest, not your head, so your back stays long.

248.cue: Front heel out, both knees straight, hands down. Breathe slowly.
how: Kneel in a low lunge, fingertips wide on the floor or books, just ahead of the front foot.
Slide the front heel forward, toes up, until that knee is straight.
Slide the back leg back and straighten it, the back kneecap facing the floor.
Stop about 30 cm from the floor and breathe slowly, then bend the front knee to come out.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
248.name: Front split prep
248.setup: 2 m of clear floor, two books for your hands.
248.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or a tug high under the buttock; never bounce.
tips: Keep your hips square: back toes on the floor, front toes pointing up.
Take your weight in your hands so you can rise at any moment.
30 cm is about the long side of a sheet of printer paper.

249.cue: Slide lower, knees straight, hips square, hands down. Breathe slowly.
how: Kneel in a low lunge, hands wide on the floor or books, just ahead of the front foot.
Slide the front heel forward, toes up, and the back knee back, both legs straight.
Lower slowly, your hands taking your weight, the back kneecap facing the floor.
Stop about 15 cm from the floor and breathe slowly, then bend the front knee to come out.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
249.name: Low front split
249.setup: 2 m of clear floor, two books for your hands.
249.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or a tug high under the buttock; never bounce.
tips: 15 cm is about the width of one and a half fists.
Slide down slowly and never drop or bounce into the split.
Keep your hips square: back toes on the floor, front toes pointing up.

25.cue: Squat, jump, land softly on the balls of your feet. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and check nothing hangs low above your head.
Squat down to about chair height and swing your arms back behind you.
Swing your arms up and jump straight up, reaching for the ceiling.
Breathe out as you jump, land on the balls of your feet and sink into your knees.
Stand up tall, count the rep out loud, then start the next jump.
25.name: Squat jump
25.setup: Clear space, shoes on, a floor that does not slip.
25.stop: Stop when your landings get loud or your knees cave in.
tips: Land as quietly as you can, rolling from the balls of your feet down to your heels.
Keep your knees pointing over your toes both on take-off and on landing.
Reset to standing tall before each jump, one clean jump at a time.

250.cue: Both thighs down, hips square, sit tall, hands down. Breathe slowly.
how: Start in a low lunge, hands wide on the floor or books, just ahead of the front foot.
Slide the front heel forward and the back knee back, both knees straight.
Lower until both thighs rest on the floor, your hands taking your weight.
Sit tall with your hips square and breathe slowly, then bend the front knee to come out.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
250.name: Front split
250.setup: 2 m of clear floor, two books by your hips.
250.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or a tug high under the buttock; never bounce.
tips: Rest your hips on the books if they stop short of the floor.
Keep the back kneecap facing the floor and the front toes pointing up.
Slide down slowly and never drop or bounce into the split.

251.cue: Bend one knee, hips back, other leg straight. Breathe slowly.
how: Face the desk with your fingertips on its edge and your feet five foot-lengths apart.
Turn your toes out a little and bend one knee, sending your hips back and down.
Keep the other leg straight with its heel down and its toes pointing up or ahead.
Lower until the bent thigh is level, then breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
251.name: Side lunge stretch
251.setup: Face the desk, hands on its edge, feet five foot-lengths apart.
251.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if the inside of a knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Keep the bent knee over its toes, not falling in.
Sit back as if onto a chair to keep your chest up.
Use the desk only for balance, so your legs take your weight.

252.cue: Fold from the hips, knees straight, palms down. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your feet wide, five foot-lengths apart, toes pointing ahead.
Put your hands on your hips and hinge forward from the hips with a long, flat back.
Lower your palms to the floor or the books between your feet, under your shoulders.
Breathe slowly in the fold, knees straight.
Put your hands on your hips and rise slowly with a flat back at the end of the hold.
252.name: Wide-leg fold
252.setup: Clear floor, feet five foot-lengths apart, two books in front.
252.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if the inside of a knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Keep your hands on the books if the floor is too far, knees straight.
Keep your weight over the middle of your feet, not back on your heels.
Stand still for a breath after you rise, then step your feet in.

253.cue: Legs wide, kneecaps up, fold onto your forearms. Breathe slowly.
how: Sit tall on the towel and open your legs wide, at least a right angle apart.
Point your kneecaps and toes at the ceiling and keep your knees straight.
Walk your hands forward and fold from the hips with a long back.
Lower onto your forearms if they reach, then breathe slowly.
Walk your hands back to sit up at the end of the hold.
253.name: Seated straddle fold
253.setup: Sit on a folded towel, 2 m of clear floor to the sides.
253.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if the inside of a knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Tip your hips forward first, so the fold comes from the hips, not a round back.
Bring your legs a little closer if your kneecaps roll in.
Sit higher on the towel if your back rounds before you can lean.

254.cue: Legs out to the sides, kneecaps forward, hands down. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your feet wide and your hands on the floor or the books in front of you.
Slide your feet out to the sides, knees straight, kneecaps facing forward.
Lower your hips slowly, your hands taking your weight.
Stop at a strong pull or with your hips on the towel, and breathe slowly.
To come out, lean on your hands, bend your knees and walk your feet in.
254.name: Middle split
254.setup: 2 m of clear floor, a folded towel under your seat, books for your hands.
254.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if the inside of a knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Keep your kneecaps facing forward or up, never rolling in.
Keep your weight in your hands so you can rise at any moment.
Slide down slowly and never drop or bounce into the split.

255.cue: Legs wide, kneecaps up, chest down towards the floor. Breathe slowly.
how: Sit tall on the towel with your legs wide, at least a right angle apart.
Point your kneecaps and toes up and keep both knees straight.
Tip your hips forward and walk your hands out, chest leading.
Lower your chest and chin to the floor if they reach, and breathe slowly.
Walk your hands back to sit up at the end of the hold.
255.name: Pancake
255.setup: Sit on a folded towel, 2 m of clear floor to the sides.
255.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if the inside of a knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Fold from the hips, since a round back only brings your head down.
Hold your feet or reach your arms ahead, whichever keeps your knees straight.
Bring your legs a little closer if your kneecaps roll in.

256.cue: Heel down, toes up, hinge forward, then let your back round. Breathe slowly.
how: Sit near the front edge of your chair with both feet flat.
Slide one foot forward until that leg is straight, heel down and toes up.
Hinge from your hips, then let your back round as your hands slide down the leg.
Reach for the ankle with the knee straight, then breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
256.name: Chair hamstring stretch
256.setup: Sit near the front edge of your chair, feet flat.
256.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or any tingling down the leg; never bounce.
tips: Lead with your chest, not your head, so the stretch stays behind the thigh.
Keep both sit bones on the chair and the other foot flat.
Rest your hands on the shin if the ankle is too far.

257.cue: Hook your big toes, knees straight, head hanging. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your knees a little bent.
Fold from the hips and hook each big toe with two fingers and the thumb.
Straighten your knees and lift your chest to make your back long.
Breathe slowly, then let your chest fold down towards your legs.
Let go, bend your knees and rise slowly at the end of the hold.
257.name: Big toe fold
257.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or any tingling down the leg; never bounce.
tips: Bend your knees as much as you need to reach the toes, then straighten them.
Pull on the toes only gently, never to force the fold.
Keep your weight over the balls of your feet, not back on your heels.

258.cue: Legs straight, fold from the hips, hold your soles. Breathe slowly.
how: Sit tall on the towel with your legs straight and together, toes up.
Reach your arms up to make your back long.
Fold forward from the hips and hold the soles of your feet.
Keep the backs of your knees on the floor and breathe slowly.
Walk your hands back along your legs to sit up at the end of the hold.
258.name: Seated forward fold
258.setup: Sit on a folded towel on the floor.
258.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or any tingling down the leg; never bounce.
tips: Loop a towel round your feet if your hands do not reach the soles.
Grow long on each breath in and fold a little lower on each breath out.
Fold from the hips, since a round back only brings your head down.

259.cue: Palms beside your feet, forehead to your knees. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your feet together and your knees a little bent.
Fold from the hips and put your palms flat beside your feet.
Straighten your knees and draw your forehead in towards them.
Breathe slowly, letting the fold deepen on each breath out.
Bend your knees and rise slowly at the end of the hold.
259.name: Forehead to knees fold
259.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or any tingling down the leg; never bounce.
tips: Bend your elbows back to draw your chest closer to your legs.
Keep your weight forward over the balls of your feet, not back on your heels.
Stand still for a breath after you rise before you move on.

26.cue: Step back slowly, back knee toward the floor. Count out loud, breathe out as you rise.
how: Stand side-on to the desk, feet hip-width apart, close enough to touch the edge.
Stand tall with your weight on one foot, chest up and arms loose at your sides.
Take one long step back, then lower for 2 s until the back knee hovers above the floor.
Breathe in on the way down and out as you push through the front heel to stand.
Each return to standing counts one; finish one side, press Switch sides, then the other.
26.name: Slow reverse lunge
26.setup: The desk within reach for balance.
26.stop: Stop when your front knee caves in. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep the front heel down and push through it, so the front leg does the work.
Step back far enough that the front shin stays close to upright at the bottom.
Fix your eyes on a spot ahead at eye level to stay steady on the way down.

260.cue: Chest on your thighs, chin to your shins, knees down. Breathe slowly.
how: Sit tall with your legs straight and together, toes up.
Reach your arms up, then fold forward from the hips.
Clasp your hands beyond your soles, or hold your feet.
Lay your chest on your thighs and your chin on your shins, and breathe slowly.
Walk your hands back up your legs to sit up at the end of the hold.
260.name: Pike fold
260.setup: Sit on the floor, legs straight and together.
260.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or any tingling down the leg; never bounce.
tips: Keep the backs of your knees on the floor the whole time.
Bend your elbows out to the sides to draw your chest along your thighs.
Fold from the hips, since a round back only brings your head down.

261.cue: Hands on your low back, lift your chest, look up. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft, hips over your feet.
Put your palms on your low back, fingers pointing down.
Lift your chest up and back while your hips stay over your feet.
Let your eyes go to the ceiling and breathe slowly.
Rise slowly, chest leading, at the end of the hold.
261.name: Standing backbend
261.setup: Clear space, feet hip-width, the desk within reach.
261.stop: Ease off if your low back pinches or your neck hurts; never bounce.
tips: Think of lifting your chest up, not of bending your low back.
Squeeze your seat so your hips stay over your feet.
Keep your neck long and let your head follow your chest, never dropping back hard.

262.cue: Hips over knees, lift your chest, hands to your heels. Breathe slowly.
how: Kneel tall with your knees hip-width apart and your thighs upright.
Put your hands on your low back and lift your chest up.
Lean back from the chest, hips over your knees, and reach your hands to your heels.
Breathe slowly with your neck long.
Bring your hands back to your low back, then rise slowly, chest first.
262.name: Camel
262.setup: Kneel on a folded towel, hands on your low back before you lean.
262.stop: Ease off if your low back pinches or your neck hurts; never bounce.
tips: Tuck your toes under to raise your heels closer to your hands.
Keep pressing your hips forward so your thighs stay upright.
Stay with your hands on your back, chest lifted, if your heels are too far.

263.cue: Hands by your ears, press up five times, arms and legs long. Breathe slowly.
how: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart near your seat.
Put your hands by your ears, fingers pointing to your feet, elbows up.
Lift your hips, set the top of your head down lightly, then press your arms straight.
Lift your head off the floor, push your legs as straight as they go, and breathe slowly.
Tuck your chin, lower slowly and press up again: five times, the last held 20 s.
263.name: Wheel
263.setup: A clear 2 x 2 m floor that does not slip and a wall behind you.
263.stop: Come down slowly, chin tucked, if your arms shake or your low back pinches.
tips: Keep your knees and feet pointing forward, not turning out.
Press the floor away through your hands to open your shoulders.
Come down at once, chin tucked, if your arms start to give.

264.cue: Lean back, walk your hands down the wall and back up. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your back to the wall, a long step away, feet hip-width apart.
Raise your arms, lean back and put your palms on the wall, fingers pointing down.
Walk your hands down the wall, chest lifting and hips pressing forward.
Set your hands on the floor in the wheel, then walk back up the wall the same way.
Go down and up five times at an easy pace, breathing slowly.
264.name: Wall walk to wheel
264.setup: A clear 2 x 2 m floor and a wall behind you, a long step away.
264.stop: Stop and walk back up if your arms shake or your low back pinches.
tips: Walk your hands in small steps and keep your hips pressing forward.
Your head is closest to the floor at the bottom, so go slowly there.
Walk back up as soon as your arms start to tire.

265.cue: Arch back to the wheel, then rock up to standing. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the clear floor behind you.
Lift your chest, press your hips forward and raise your arms over your head.
Arch back slowly, eyes on the floor behind you, and set your hands down.
Rock your weight onto your feet, press through your legs and rise to standing.
Go down and up three times, breathing slowly.
265.name: Stand-to-stand wheel
265.setup: A clear 2 x 2 m floor that does not slip and a wall behind you for first tries.
265.stop: Stop and lower to the floor if your arms shake or your low back pinches.
tips: Keep your hips pressing forward on the way down so your hands land, not your head.
Use the wall to walk down and up until you can do it without it.
Rock a few times in the wheel to move your weight onto your feet before you rise.

266.cue: Sit tall, turn your chest, knees forward. Breathe out as you turn.
how: Sit tall on your chair facing the desk, knees together and feet flat.
Breathe in and grow tall through the top of your head.
Breathe out and turn your chest to one side, knees still facing forward.
Hold the chair back with the hand behind you and the desk edge with the other.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
266.name: Chair twist
266.setup: Sit tall on your chair facing the desk, feet flat.
266.stop: Ease off if your back pinches; never pull to turn further.
tips: Grow taller on each breath in and turn a little further on each breath out.
Keep both sit bones heavy on the chair as your chest turns.
Turn your chest first and let your head follow last.

267.cue: Palms together, elbow outside the far knee. Breathe out to turn.
how: Stand with your feet together and sit back as if onto a chair.
Press your palms together at your chest.
Breathe out and turn, hooking one elbow outside the other knee.
Keep your knees level and breathe slowly, growing long on each breath in.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
267.name: Twisted chair pose
267.setup: Feet together, the desk within reach.
267.stop: Ease off if your back pinches or a knee hurts; never pull to turn further.
tips: Keep your knees side by side, since the one you hook will want to slide ahead.
Press your palms together to turn your chest towards the ceiling.
Keep your weight in your heels, so you could lift your toes.

268.cue: Hips square, knees straight, top arm up. Breathe out to turn.
how: Step one foot back a leg-length, back toes turned out a little, hips facing forward.
Reach the arm on the back-leg side forward and hinge over the front leg with a flat back.
Put that palm on the floor or the book outside the front foot.
Breathe out and turn your chest open, top arm reaching straight up.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
268.name: Twisted triangle
268.setup: Clear floor, feet a leg-length apart, a book by your front foot.
268.stop: Ease off if your back pinches; never pull to turn further.
tips: Draw the front hip back so your hips stay level as you turn.
Use the book or set the hand inside the foot if the floor is too far.
Look down at the floor if looking up bothers your neck.

269.cue: Arm round the knee, clasp behind your back. Breathe out to turn.
how: Sit tall with one leg long and the other knee bent, its foot flat by the long thigh.
Breathe in and grow tall, then breathe out and turn towards the bent knee.
Wrap the opposite arm round the outside of the bent knee.
Reach the other hand behind your back, clasp your fingers and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
269.name: Bound seated twist
269.setup: Sit tall on a folded towel on the floor.
269.stop: Ease off if your back pinches; never pull on the bind.
tips: Hold a towel between your hands if your fingers do not meet.
Keep the long leg flat on the floor and both sit bones down.
Sit tall before each turn and never twist with a round back.

27.cue: Step wide, sit into one hip, the other leg straight. Breathe out as you push back.
how: Stand with a clear metre on each side of you, feet hip-width apart.
Stand tall, then step one foot out until your feet are about twice shoulder-width apart.
Sit your hips back over that foot, the other leg straight, arms forward.
Breathe in as you sink, then breathe out as you push off that foot back to the start.
Each return to the start counts one; finish one side, press Switch sides, then the other.
27.name: Lateral lunge
27.setup: A clear step to each side.
27.stop: Stop when your knee passes your toes or caves in. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep both feet flat and pointing forward, the heel of the bent leg pressed down.
Push your hips back as if closing a drawer behind you, rather than dropping straight down.
Feel a stretch along the inside of the straight leg as you sit into the bent one.

270.cue: Turn, arm round the front thigh, clasp behind your back. Breathe out.
how: Step into a long lunge, front knee over the ankle, back knee straight.
Press your palms together and turn, hooking the far elbow outside the front knee.
Thread that arm under the front thigh and reach the other hand behind your back.
Clasp your hands or the towel behind you, chest turned up, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
270.name: Bound lunge twist
270.setup: A long stride of clear floor, a towel ready for your hands.
270.stop: Ease off if your back pinches or a knee hurts; never pull on the bind.
tips: Drop the back knee to the floor while you find the clasp, then lift it again.
Hold the towel between your hands if your fingers do not meet.
Grow tall on each breath in and turn a little on each breath out.

271.cue: Sit deep, heels down, hands light on the desk. Breathe slowly.
how: Face the desk with your hands on its edge and your feet hip-width apart.
Turn your toes out a little and sit your hips down between your heels.
Sink until your thighs are below level, heels flat on the floor.
Let your hands rest lightly on the desk and breathe slowly.
Stand up slowly, using the desk, at the end of the hold.
271.name: Deep squat at the desk
271.setup: Face the desk, hands on its edge, feet hip-width.
271.stop: Ease off at a pinch at the front of the ankle or if a knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Push your knees out over your toes to make room for your hips.
Put a rolled towel under your heels if they lift.
Hold the desk only for balance, so your legs take your weight.

272.cue: Heels down, palms together, elbows inside the knees. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your toes turned out a little.
Sit your hips down between your heels until your thighs are below level.
Press your palms together at your chest, elbows inside your knees.
Keep your heels flat and your chest up, and breathe slowly.
Put your hands on the floor and stand up slowly at the end of the hold.
272.name: Deep squat
272.setup: Clear floor, feet hip-width, toes turned out a little.
272.stop: Ease off at a pinch at the front of the ankle or if a knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Press your elbows gently into your knees to open them over your toes.
Put a rolled towel under your heels if they lift.
Lift your chest so your back stays long, not rounded.

273.cue: Feet and knees together, heels down, hold your ankles. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your feet and knees together.
Sit your hips down low, keeping your heels flat.
Lean your chest forward over your knees and hold your ankles from behind.
Breathe slowly and let your head drop towards your toes.
Put your hands on the floor and stand up slowly at the end of the hold.
273.name: Feet-together squat
273.setup: Clear floor, feet together, a rolled towel at hand.
273.stop: Ease off at a pinch at the front of the ankle or if a knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Put the rolled towel under your heels if they lift.
Reach your arms forward for balance if you tip back.
Keep your knees together and pointing straight ahead.

274.cue: Heels down, arms round your shins, clasp behind. Breathe slowly.
how: Squat with your feet and knees together and your heels flat.
Lean forward and wrap your arms round your shins from the front.
Clasp your hands behind your calves, or hold the towel between them.
Let your head drop forward over your knees and breathe slowly.
Let go, put your hands on the floor and stand up slowly.
274.name: Bound squat
274.setup: Clear floor, feet together, a towel ready for your hands.
274.stop: Ease off at a pinch at the front of the ankle or if a knee hurts; never bounce.
tips: Put a rolled towel under your heels if they lift.
Keep your weight over your feet so you do not rock back.
Let your breath fold you in, never a pull on the clasp.

275.cue: Heels down, far arm round both thighs, clasp behind. Breathe out.
how: Squat with your feet and knees together and your heels flat.
Breathe out and turn your chest to one side, the far arm outside both knees.
Wrap that arm round both thighs and reach the other hand behind your back.
Clasp your hands or the towel behind you and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
275.name: Bound squat twist
275.setup: Clear floor, feet together, a towel ready for your hands.
275.stop: Ease off at a pinch at the front of the ankle or in your back; never bounce.
tips: Put a rolled towel under your heels if they lift.
Squat with your back near a wall while you learn, in case you tip back.
Turn on each breath out and never pull on the clasp to go further.

276.cue: Sit low, wrap the legs, cross the arms at the elbows. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk and bend your knees a little.
Cross one thigh over the other and hook the top toes behind the calf, or let them hang.
Cross your arms at the elbows and rest each hand on the opposite shoulder.
Sit a little lower, lift your elbows to shoulder height and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
276.name: Eagle
276.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, a hand's reach from it.
276.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your knee hurts.
tips: Let the top foot hang if the hook will not come; never force it.
Fix your eyes on one still spot to steady your balance.
Squeeze your thighs together to lock the pose in place.

277.cue: Arms, body and back leg in one level line. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk and reach both arms up beside your ears.
Shift your weight onto one foot and lift the other foot behind you.
Tip forward from the hip as the back leg rises, until arms, body and leg are level.
Keep the standing leg straight, hips level, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
277.name: Warrior III
277.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, fingertips within reach of it.
277.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your back pinches.
tips: Rest your fingertips on the desk while you find the line, then lift them.
Point the back toes at the floor so your hips stay level.
Reach long through your hands and your back heel, as if pulled both ways.

278.cue: Foot on the calf, hands together, eyes closed. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk, feet together, fingertips hovering just above it.
Lift one foot and set its sole on your inner calf, below the knee.
Bring your hands together at your chest and find your balance.
Close your eyes for 10 s or more and breathe slowly, keeping still.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
278.name: Tree pose, eyes closed
278.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, fingertips just over it.
278.stop: Open your eyes and put the foot down when you sway.
tips: Fix your eyes on one spot first, then close them once you are steady.
Press the foot and the calf into each other to stay steady.
Keep your standing knee soft, not locked.

279.cue: Hold the big toe, leg straight at hip height. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with the desk beside your standing leg and one hand on your hip.
Lift the other knee and hook its big toe with two fingers and the thumb.
Straighten that leg out in front of you, up to hip height.
Stand tall on a straight standing leg and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
279.name: Standing big toe hold
279.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, a towel at hand.
279.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your back rounds.
tips: Loop the towel round the foot or keep the knee bent until the leg will straighten.
Keep both hips level, since the raised hip will want to lift.
Fix your eyes on one still spot ahead to steady your balance.

28.cue: Step back and across, hips square. Count out loud, breathe out as you rise.
how: Stand with feet hip-width apart, hands on your hips, the desk close enough to touch.
Step one foot back and across behind the other, landing on the ball of that foot.
Lower until the back knee hovers above the floor, hips facing ahead.
Breathe in on the way down and out as you push through the front heel to stand.
Each return to standing counts one; finish one side, press Switch sides, then the other.
28.name: Curtsy lunge
28.setup: The desk within reach for balance.
28.stop: Stop when your front knee caves in. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep your hips square, as if lights on your hip bones shine straight ahead.
Step the foot well back, not only across, so the front knee stays over the front foot.
Keep most of your weight in the front heel and use the back foot only for balance.

280.cue: Both hands hold the back foot overhead, thigh level. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand facing the wall, bend one knee and hold that foot behind you.
Loop the towel round the foot if your hands cannot both reach it.
Take the foot or the towel in both hands over your head, elbows pointing up.
Kick the foot back into your hands and tip your chest forward until the thigh is level.
Breathe slowly; the clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
280.name: Dancer
280.setup: Face a wall an arm's length away, a towel at hand.
280.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your low back pinches.
tips: Walk your hands down the towel a little closer to the foot each time.
Keep the standing knee straight and your hips square to the wall.
Kick the foot into your hands rather than pulling with your arms.

281.cue: Arms straight, lean your shoulders past your wrists. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand a step back from the desk and put your palms flat on its edge, shoulder-width apart.
Point your fingers away from you and spread them wide.
Keep your arms and body straight and lean forward until your shoulders pass your wrists.
Breathe slowly in the lean, then ease back.
Lean in and ease back at a slow pace for the time shown.
281.name: Wrist lean at the desk
281.setup: A steady desk, palms flat on it, fingers pointing away from you.
281.stop: Ease off at once if a wrist hurts.
tips: Press the whole hand into the desk, most of all the base of the first finger.
Lean a little further over the days, only as far as your wrists stay easy.
Check that the desk stays steady before you lean your weight on it.

282.cue: Shins on your upper arms, heels up, lean forward. Breathe slowly.
how: Squat with your feet close together and your knees wide.
Put your palms flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart, fingers spread.
Bend your elbows a little and rest your shins high on your upper arms.
Rise onto your toes and lean forward until your weight is in your hands.
Breathe slowly in the lean, then lower your heels at the end of the hold.
282.name: Crow prep
282.setup: Squat on the floor, a pillow in front of your hands.
282.stop: Ease off if a wrist or a knee hurts.
tips: Look at the floor a little in front of your hands, not at your feet.
Squeeze your knees into your arms so they stay put.
Press the floor away so your upper back rounds a little.

283.cue: Knees on upper arms, lean forward, lift both feet. Breathe slowly.
how: Start in crow prep: hands flat, shins high on your upper arms, heels up.
Lean forward until your toes grow light.
Lift one foot, then the other, and draw your heels towards your seat.
Hold with your eyes ahead of your hands and breathe slowly.
Lower your feet to the floor slowly at the end of the hold.
283.name: Crow
283.setup: A pillow on the floor in front of your hands in case you tip forward.
283.stop: Come down at once if a wrist or an elbow hurts.
tips: Lift one foot at a time until both come up together.
Press the floor away and round your upper back a little.
Look forward at the floor, not down at your hands.

284.cue: Forearms down, legs straight up, heels off the walls. Breathe slowly.
how: Kneel facing the corner and set your forearms on the blanket, fingers laced.
Set the top of your head on the blanket, the back of it in your hands.
Lift your knees and walk your feet in until your hips are over your shoulders.
Draw one knee in, then the other, then straighten both legs up and breathe slowly.
Bend your knees, lower one foot, then the other, and rest in child's pose.
284.name: Headstand
284.setup: Corner of two walls, a folded blanket, head a hand from each wall.
284.stop: Come down at once if your neck hurts.
tips: Press your forearms down so your neck takes less of your weight.
Use the walls to steady your heels, then bring them off when you can.
Keep your shoulders lifted away from your ears the whole time.

285.cue: Turn, knees stacked on one arm, lean forward, lift. Breathe slowly.
how: Squat on your toes with your feet and knees together.
Turn your knees to one side and put your hands flat on the floor on that side.
Bend your elbows and rest the side of your knees on one upper arm.
Lean forward, lift both feet off the floor and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
285.name: Side crow
285.setup: A pillow on the floor in front of and beside your hands in case you tip.
285.stop: Come down at once if a wrist or an elbow hurts.
tips: Squeeze your knees together so they stay stacked.
Lift one foot at a time, or rest the lower foot on a book, until both lift.
Look forward at the floor, not down at your hands.

286.cue: Front leg over the arm, back leg long, lean and lift. Breathe slowly.
how: Start in a lunge with your hands flat on the floor inside the front foot.
Slide the front shoulder under the front thigh, close to the knee.
Bend your elbows, lean forward and walk the front foot out until that leg is straight.
Lift the back leg straight off the floor, both feet up, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
286.name: Flying splits
286.setup: A pillow on the floor in front of your hands in case you tip forward.
286.stop: Come down at once if a wrist, an elbow or a hip hurts.
tips: Lean forward only as far as you can press back up.
Lift the front foot first and keep the back toes down until it is steady.
Reach back through the back heel and keep the front knee straight.

287.cue: Hinge on one leg, the weight hanging, back flat. Count out loud, breathe out as you rise.
how: Stand side-on to the desk and hold the weight by its handle in the hand away from it.
Stand on the leg nearer the desk, knee soft, the nearer hand's fingertips on its edge.
Tip from the hip as the free leg reaches back and the weight sinks low.
Breathe in as you tip forward and breathe out as you squeeze your seat to stand tall.
Count each stand; every rep on one leg, press Switch sides, turn round and swap hands.
287.name: Single-leg deadlift with a weight
287.setup: A weight of 5-15 kg in one hand, the desk within reach.

setups.dumbbells: A dumbbell of 5-15 kg in one hand, the desk within reach.
setups.kettlebell: A kettlebell of 5-15 kg in one hand, the desk within reach.

287.stop: Stop when your hips twist or your back rounds. Count the weaker side.
tips: Pick a weight where 10 reps a leg are work and 20 hard: the game says when to go heavier.
A bag of books or bottles, a full jug, a kettlebell or dumbbell: 1 L of water weighs 1 kg.
Keep a straight line from your head to your back heel, like a seesaw.

288.cue: Lower for 3 seconds on one leg, back flat. Count out loud, breathe out as you rise.
how: Lay a thick book flat beside the desk and stand on it with the leg nearer the desk.
Hold the weight in the hand away from the desk and rest the other hand's fingertips on it.
Tip from the hip for a slow 3 s, free leg back, until the weight nearly brushes the floor.
Breathe in as you lower and breathe out as you squeeze your seat to stand tall.
Count each stand; every rep on one leg, press Switch sides, turn round and swap hands.
288.name: Slow single-leg deadlift with a weight
288.setup: A thick book to stand on, a weight of 5-15 kg in one hand, the desk within reach.

setups.dumbbells: A thick book to stand on, a 5-15 kg dumbbell in one hand, the desk within reach.
setups.kettlebell: A thick book to stand on, a 5-15 kg kettlebell in one hand, the desk within reach.

288.stop: Stop when you lose the 3-s lowering or your back rounds. Count the weaker side.
tips: Take your single-leg deadlift's weight: 10 slow reps a leg should be work, 20 hard.
The book lets the weight sink lower, so stop where your back starts to round.
Pick a hardback that lies flat and does not slide on your floor.

289.cue: Thighs nearly level, one leg straight out. Count out loud.
how: Stand with your back to the wall, feet hip-width apart and heels about 60 cm out.
Slide down until your thighs are nearly level with the floor, knees over your ankles.
Straighten one leg out in front, its heel just off the floor, and hold on the other.
Hold still and breathe slowly in and out, your head and back flat on the wall.
Count out loud; when this side ends, press Switch sides, then change legs.
289.name: Single-leg wall sit, 105 degrees
289.setup: Back flat on the wall, nothing slippery underfoot.
289.stop: Stop when you slide or your knee aches. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep the standing knee over its ankle and pointing straight ahead, not caving in.
Let the free leg hover low, since holding it high only tires your hip.
Press the whole standing foot into the floor, heel too, so you do not slide.

29.cue: Step back, then drive that knee up high. Breathe out on the drive.
how: Stand beside the desk with feet hip-width apart, close enough to touch the edge.
Step one foot back into a lunge, both knees bent, chest tall over your hips.
Drive the back knee up to hip height as the opposite arm swings forward.
Breathe in as you step back and breathe out hard on the drive.
Each knee drive counts one; finish one side, press Switch sides, then do the other.
29.name: Step-back knee drive
29.setup: The desk within reach for balance.
29.stop: Stop when you lose your balance. Count the weaker side.
tips: Stand tall on the standing leg at the top, hips pushed forward, not leaning back.
Fix your eyes on one spot ahead to hold your balance on one leg.
Make the drive fast but the step back soft and under control.

290.cue: Thighs level, one leg straight out. Count out loud.
how: Stand with your back to the wall, feet hip-width apart and heels about 60 cm out.
Slide down until your thighs are level with the floor, knees right over your ankles.
Straighten one leg out in front, its heel just off the floor, and hold on the other.
Hold still and breathe slowly in and out, your head and back flat on the wall.
Count out loud; when this side ends, press Switch sides, then change legs.
290.name: Single-leg wall sit, 90 degrees
290.setup: Back flat on the wall, nothing slippery underfoot.
290.stop: Stop when you slide or your knee aches. Count the weaker side.
tips: Picture the standing shin straight up and down and its thigh flat like a table top.
Push the standing heel into the floor to keep your back from sliding down the wall.
Breathe out on every count so your breath keeps moving as the hold gets hard.

291.cue: Each knee up to the other hand, fast. Breathe out on every drive.
how: Stand tall in the cleared space, feet hip-width apart, hands up in front of your chest.
Drive your right knee up and across while your left hand comes down to meet it.
Set the foot down and drive the left knee up to the right hand at once.
Keep switching as fast as you stay balanced, turning from your waist.
Go fast enough that you cannot say a full sentence.
291.name: Cross-knee drives
291.setup: Clear a small space beside the desk.
tips: Bring the knee up to the hand, never the hand down to the knee.
Keep the standing knee soft and your chest up as you turn.

292.cue: Tiny, fast steps, one foot always down, arms pumping. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft, weight on the balls of your feet.
Take tiny, fast steps on the spot, lifting each heel while the toes stay down.
Keep one foot on the floor at all times, so you never hop or land.
Pump your bent arms fast in time with your feet.
Go as fast as you can keep it quiet, too fast to talk.
292.name: Quick steps
292.setup: Shoes on, a floor that does not slip.
tips: Faster, not higher: the quicker your feet, the harder it gets.
Stay light and quiet, with no stamping.

293.cue: Squat, then drive up onto your toes, arms overhead. Breathe out as you rise.
how: Fill the backpack with books or bottles, 3 to 8 kg, and wear it on both straps, snug.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms at your sides.
Sit back and down into a squat, chest up, arms reaching forward.
Drive up fast onto your toes and reach both arms straight overhead.
Drop your heels and sit straight into the next squat, too fast to talk.

vest: Put on the vest, 3 to 8 kg, and close it snug so it does not bounce.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms at your sides.
Sit back and down into a squat, chest up, arms reaching forward.
Drive up fast onto your toes and reach both arms straight overhead.
Drop your heels and sit straight into the next squat, too fast to talk.

293.name: Backpack squat drives
293.setup: A packed backpack, 3-8 kg, on both straps.

setups.backpack: A packed backpack, 3-8 kg, on both straps.
setups.vest: A weighted vest of 3-8 kg, snug and even.

tips: Let the drive come from your legs; the arms only follow.
Take a lighter pack if your squats get shallow before the time is up.

30.cue: Hop sideways from foot to foot, land softly; each landing counts one. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Clear about a metre to each side and stand on one foot, knee bent, chest leaning forward.
Let the other foot hang behind and across your standing ankle, off the floor.
Push off sideways and land softly on the other foot, swinging your arms across your body.
Let the free foot sweep behind the landing leg, then push straight back the other way.
Breathe in rhythm with the hops at a hard pace, too fast to talk.
30.name: Skater hops
30.setup: A clear step to each side, a floor that does not slip.
30.stop: Stop if your landings get loud.
tips: Land on the ball of the foot and sink into the knee to make each landing quiet.
Land balanced over the foot, so each push starts from a steady leg.
Keep your chest over the landing knee rather than letting it tip to the outside.

300.cue: Lower on one arm for 3 seconds, push up on both. Count out loud, breathe steadily.
how: Start on your toes with both hands on the floor, then walk your feet out very wide.
Put one hand under the middle of your chest and rest the other on your lower back.
Bend the elbow and lower your chest to just above the floor over three slow beats.
At the bottom set the free hand down, breathe out and push up on both arms.
Each lowering is one. One arm, press Switch sides, the other; type the weaker arm's count.
300.name: One-arm lowering
300.setup: On the floor, feet wide; one hand under your chest, the other behind your back.
300.stop: Stop when you drop fast or your hips twist. Count the weaker side.
tips: Squeeze your seat and brace your belly so your hips stay level with your shoulders.
Keep the working elbow close to your side, pointing back towards your hip.
Say the beats out loud so the last part of the way down stays slow.

301.cue: Lower and push up on one arm, hips level. Count out loud, breathe out as you push.
how: Start in a push-up on the floor, feet together, body straight from heels to head.
Put one hand under the middle of your chest and rest the other on your lower back.
Lower your chest towards the floor, hips and shoulders level.
Breathe out and push the floor away until your arm is straight.
Each push-up is one. One arm, press Switch sides, the other; type the weaker arm's count.
301.name: One-arm push-up, feet together
301.setup: On the floor, feet together; one hand under your chest, the other behind your back.
301.stop: Stop when your hips twist or sag. Count the weaker side.
tips: Lean your weight a little over the working hand before you bend the elbow.
Brace your belly and seat hard before each rep so your hips cannot turn open.
Keep the elbow close to your ribs and grip the floor with spread fingers.

302.cue: Back foot up behind you, sit until the knee taps the cushion. Count out loud, breathe out.
how: Put the cushion just behind the heel you stand on, with the desk in reach at your side.
Stand on one leg, bend the other knee so that foot lifts behind you, arms forward.
Lean your chest forward and sit back until the back knee taps the cushion.
Keep the back foot off the floor, breathe out and stand up on the front leg.
Each stand is one. One leg, press Switch sides, the other; type the weaker leg's count.
302.name: Shrimp squat
302.setup: A cushion behind you for the back knee; the desk within reach.
302.stop: Stop when the knee drops fast or caves in. Count the weaker side.
tips: Reach your arms further forward as you sink; they balance the leg behind you.
Keep the front heel flat and the front knee pointing over your toes.
Touch the cushion as softly as you can, with no bounce off it.

303.cue: Sit all the way down on one leg, wait 2 seconds, stand. Count out loud, breathe steadily.
how: Stand in clear space with the desk just within reach at your side to catch yourself.
Stand on one leg, reach both arms forward and lift the other leg straight out in front.
Sit down on the standing leg all the way to the bottom, heel flat, taking about 2 s.
Stay tight at the bottom for 2 s, free leg off the floor, then breathe out and stand.
Each stand is one. One leg, press Switch sides, the other; type the weaker leg's count.
303.name: Pistol squat with a pause
303.setup: Clear space; the desk within reach to catch yourself.
303.stop: Stop when your heel lifts or your knee caves in. Count the weaker side.
tips: Say the two beats out loud at the bottom, which keeps you breathing.
Stay tight in the pause; do not relax and rest at the bottom.
Reach your arms forward and keep your chest up so you do not roll back.

304.cue: Foot held behind you, sit until the knee taps the cushion. Count out loud, breathe out.
how: Put the cushion just behind the heel you stand on and stand on one leg in clear space.
Bend the other knee and hold that foot behind your seat with the same side's hand.
