570.name: Bound squat twist, press and sink
570.setup: Clear floor, feet together, a towel ready for your hands.
570.stop: Ease off at a pinch at the front of the ankle or in your back; never bounce.
tips: Half effort is enough; never pull on the clasp to turn.
Keep breathing through each press; never hold your breath.
Put a rolled towel under your heels if they lift.

571.cue: Heels down, armpit past both knees, arms reaching, hands free. Breathe out.
how: Squat with your feet and knees together and your heels flat.
Breathe out and turn until the far armpit passes the outside of both knees.
Reach that arm down past your shins and the other arm back behind you.
Hold the turn with your own muscles, hands touching nothing, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
571.name: Squat twist, arms reaching
571.setup: Clear floor, feet together, a rolled towel at hand.
571.stop: Ease off at a pinch at the front of the ankle or in your back; never bounce.
tips: Put the rolled towel under your heels if they lift; the goal pose needs them flat.
Turn a little more on each breath out; never swing into the turn.
It builds the turn the bound squat twist needs before the hands meet.

576.cue: On one foot, turn your head slowly from side to side. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk, feet together, fingertips hovering just above it.
Shift onto one foot, bend the other knee and lift that foot behind you, shin level.
Put your hands on your hips and fix your eyes on a spot ahead.
Turn your head slowly to one side, then the other, and keep turning the whole hold.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch feet.
576.name: One-leg stand, head turns
576.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, fingertips just over it.
576.stop: Put the foot down when you sway.
tips: Turn slowly, about two seconds each way, and let your eyes travel with your head.
Keep your hips level and your standing knee soft, not locked.
Turn less far if you feel dizzy; small turns still train your balance.

577.cue: Hug one knee to your chest and stand tall on the other leg. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk, a hand's reach from it, feet together.
Shift onto one foot and lift the other knee up in front of you.
Wrap both arms round the shin and hug the knee in towards your chest.
Stand tall on a straight standing leg, hips level, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
577.name: Standing knee hug
577.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, a hand's reach from it.
577.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your hip pinches.
tips: Lift the knee up to your chest; do not lean down to meet it.
Fix your eyes on one still spot ahead to steady your balance.
Let one hand go to the desk if you tip, then hug the knee again.

578.cue: On the towel on one foot, thigh level, hands on hips. Breathe slowly.
how: Fold a bath towel into a thick square and lay it on the floor beside the desk.
Step onto the towel with one foot, side-on to the desk, fingertips just over it.
Lift the other knee in front of you until the thigh is level.
Put your hands on your hips and breathe slowly as the towel shifts under you.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch feet.
578.name: One-leg stand on a towel
578.setup: A bath towel folded thick on a floor that does not slip, by the desk.
578.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your ankle rolls.
tips: Let your foot make small moves on the towel; that is your balance at work.
Fix your eyes on one still spot ahead to steady yourself.
Keep the standing knee soft, not locked, and the hips level.

579.cue: Ankle over the standing knee, sit back, palms together. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk, feet together, fingertips hovering just above it.
Shift onto one foot and cross the other ankle over that knee, the crossed knee out.
Bend the standing knee and send your seat back as if to sit on a chair.
Bring your palms together at your chest, chest lifted, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
579.name: Standing figure four
579.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, fingertips just over it.
579.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or the pull in your hip grows strong.
tips: Pull the toes of the crossed foot back to keep the ankle steady on the knee.
Sit back until the crossed shin lies level, and no deeper for now.
Keep the standing knee over your toes, not falling in.

58.cue: Pull as if to row, elbows back, and hold. Count out loud.
how: Face the edge of a solid doorframe and grip it at chest height, one hand above the other.
Toes close to the frame, lean back a little, heels to head in one straight line.
Pull until your elbows bend to a right angle, elbows back, and hold still there.
Keep breathing slowly and steadily through the whole hold.
Count out loud while the clock times the hold, from your first pull until you let go.
58.name: Doorframe isometric row
58.setup: Grip a solid doorframe at chest height.
58.stop: Stop when your shoulders shrug or you hold your breath.
tips: Squeeze your shoulder blades together and keep them there the whole time.
Keep your hips in line, as if your body were a stiff board leaning off the frame.
Keep your shoulders low and wide, away from your ears.

580.cue: Foot on the calf or thigh, arms up, look at the ceiling. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk, feet together, fingertips hovering just above it.
Lift one foot and set its sole on your inner calf or thigh, never on the knee.
Reach both arms straight up beside your ears, palms facing in.
Once steady, tip your head back slowly and look up at the ceiling.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch feet.
580.name: Tree pose, eyes up
580.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, fingertips just over it.
580.stop: Put the foot down when you sway.
tips: Find one still spot on the ceiling to look at, as you would ahead.
Tip your head back only as far as your neck is happy to go.
Press the foot and the leg into each other to lock the pose in place.

581.cue: Hand on the books, top leg level, hips stacked, top arm up. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your feet wide, the books by your front foot, the desk a step behind you.
Bend the front knee and put that hand on the books, a foot's length past the toes.
Shift onto the front foot and lift the back leg until it is level with the floor.
Straighten the standing leg, stack the top hip over the bottom one, top arm up.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
581.name: Half moon on books
581.setup: Clear floor, books 25 cm high by your front foot, the desk behind you.
581.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your hip or back pinches.
tips: Point the top toes ahead, not up, so your hips stay stacked.
Look at the floor while you find the line, then turn your eyes to the side.
Press the books lightly and let the standing leg take your weight.

582.cue: Hold the knee out to the side at hip height and stand tall. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk, the desk by your standing leg, feet together.
Lift the other knee in front of you and hold it from below with the same hand.
Open the knee out to the side, keeping it at hip height, the foot hanging.
Stand tall, let go, hands on your hips, and hold the knee up for 5 s.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
582.name: Knee out to the side
582.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, fingertips just over it.
582.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or the pull in your hip grows strong.
tips: Open the knee only as far as your hips stay level.
Keep your chest facing ahead as the knee turns out.
Fix your eyes on one still spot ahead to steady your balance.

583.cue: Ankle over the knee, sit back and fold your chest down. Breathe slowly.
how: Come into the standing figure four, ankle over the standing knee, palms together.
Sit back a little more and fold your chest forward over the crossed shin.
Lower the chest until it is directly over the shin, your back long.
Keep your weight in the standing heel and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
583.name: Standing figure four, folded
583.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, fingertips just over it.
583.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or the pull in your hip grows strong.
tips: Fold from the hips, never by rounding your back.
Rest your hands on the crossed shin if you wobble, then lift them again.
Pull the toes of the crossed foot back to keep the ankle steady on the knee.

584.cue: Foot on the calf or thigh, rise onto the ball of the foot. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk, feet together, fingertips hovering just above it.
Come into the tree, sole on your inner calf or thigh, hands together at your chest.
Rise slowly onto the ball of the standing foot, heel lifted high.
Hold steady at the top and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
584.name: Tree pose on tiptoe
584.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, fingertips just over it.
584.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your calf cramps.
tips: Rise straight up over the big toe, not out to the little toe.
Lower the heel for a breath and rise again if you wobble.
Fix your eyes on one still spot at eye level.

585.cue: On the towel on one foot, close your eyes for 5 s. Breathe slowly.
how: Fold a bath towel into a thick square on the floor beside the desk.
Step onto it with one foot, side-on to the desk, fingertips hovering just above it.
Lift the other foot beside the standing ankle and put your hands on your hips.
Once steady, close your eyes for 5 s or more and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch feet.
585.name: Towel stand, eyes closed
585.setup: A bath towel folded thick on a floor that does not slip, by the desk.
585.stop: Open your eyes and put the foot down when you sway.
tips: Fix your eyes on one spot first, then close them once you are steady.
Let your foot make small moves on the towel; that is your balance at work.
Open your eyes at once if you tip, and touch the desk.

586.cue: On the towel, sit low, wrap the legs, cross the arms at the elbows. Breathe slowly.
how: Fold a bath towel into a thick square on the floor beside the desk and stand on it.
Bend your knees a little and cross one thigh over the other, toes hooked or hanging.
Cross your arms at the elbows and rest each hand on the opposite shoulder.
Sit a little lower, lift your elbows to shoulder height and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
586.name: Eagle on a towel
586.setup: A bath towel folded thick on a floor that does not slip, by the desk.
586.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your knee strains.
tips: Learn the eagle on the floor first; the towel makes the same shape harder.
Squeeze your thighs together to lock the pose in place.
Let the top foot hang if the hook will not come; never force it.

587.cue: Hold the big toe and open the straight leg out to the side. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with the desk beside your standing leg and that hand on your hip.
Lift the other knee and hook its big toe with two fingers and the thumb.
Straighten the leg in front of you, then open it out to the side, foot at knee height.
Stand tall on a straight standing leg, hips level, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
587.name: Big toe hold to the side
587.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, a towel at hand.
587.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or the pull behind your knee grows strong.
tips: Loop the towel round the foot or keep the knee bent until the leg will straighten.
Keep both hips level as the leg opens, since the raised hip will want to lift.
Fix your eyes on one still spot ahead to steady your balance.

588.cue: In the half moon, lift the bottom hand just off the books. Breathe slowly.
how: Come into the half moon on books, top leg level and top arm straight up.
Shift a little more of your weight onto the standing foot.
Lift the bottom hand a hand's width off the books and hold it there.
Keep the hips stacked and the top leg level, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
588.name: Half moon, hand floating
588.setup: Clear floor, books 25 cm high by your front foot, the desk behind you.
588.stop: Come down to the books with your hand when you sway or your back pinches.
tips: Lift the hand for a breath, touch down, then lift it again for longer.
Reach long through the top heel to keep the leg level.
Keep your eyes on the floor ahead until the float feels steady.

589.cue: In the eagle, rise onto the ball of the standing foot. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand side-on to the desk and come into the eagle, sitting a little low.
Cross the thighs, hook the top toes or let them hang, and cross your arms.
Rise slowly onto the ball of the standing foot, heel lifted high.
Keep the knee bent and the thighs squeezed, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
589.name: Eagle on tiptoe
589.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, a hand's reach from it.
589.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your knee strains.
tips: Rise straight up over the big toe, not out to the little toe.
Lower the heel for a breath and rise again if you wobble.
Fix your eyes on one still spot at eye level.

59.cue: Pull your chest to the edge, lower to straight arms. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Lean on the edge, then pull gently: if the table lifts, slides or creaks, stop.
Lie under it, chest below the edge, and grip it a little wider than your shoulders.
Heels on the floor, lift your hips so your body is straight from heels to head.
Pull your chest to the edge, then lower until your arms are fully straight.
Let your back touch the floor lightly, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.
59.name: Inverted row under a table
59.setup: A heavy table on four legs; never glass, folding, a standing desk or one with monitors.
59.stop: Stop when your hips sag or the table moves.
tips: Squeeze your bottom and belly so your hips rise with your chest, not after it.
Drive your elbows down towards the floor and squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Keep your neck long, chin slightly tucked, eyes on the underside of the table.

590.cue: In the half moon, bend the top knee and hold that foot. Breathe slowly.
how: Come into the half moon on books, top leg level and top arm straight up.
Bend the top knee and reach the top hand back to hold the foot or a towel round it.
Kick the foot back into your hand until the thigh is level again.
Open your chest towards the ceiling and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
590.name: Half moon bow
590.setup: Clear floor, books 25 cm high by your front foot, the desk behind you, a towel at hand.
590.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or your low back pinches.
tips: Loop the towel round the foot first if your hand cannot reach it.
Kick the foot into your hand rather than pulling with your arm.
Keep the standing leg straight and the bottom hand a fist off the books.

591.cue: Leg straight at hip height, let go of the toe and hold it up. Breathe slowly.
how: Come into the standing big toe hold, the leg straight in front at hip height.
Stand tall on a straight standing leg, the other hand on your hip.
Let go of the toe, that hand to your hip, and hold the leg up by itself for 5 s.
Take the toe again, then lower the leg slowly and breathe.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
591.name: Leg up, no hands
591.setup: Stand side-on to the desk, a towel at hand.
591.stop: Put the foot down when you sway or the front of your hip cramps.
tips: Keep the knee straight as you let go; a high leg with a bent knee does not count.
Squeeze the front of the thigh hard to keep the leg up.
Stand tall, since leaning back to lift the leg takes the work off the hip.

596.cue: Arms straight, lean back until your forearms stretch. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand close to the desk and put your palms flat on it, shoulder-width apart.
Turn your hands so your fingers point back at you, thumbs out to the sides.
Keep your arms straight and move your hips back, your shoulders behind your wrists.
Keep the heels of your hands pressed down and breathe slowly.
Ease forward again at the end of the hold.
596.name: Reverse wrist lean at the desk
596.setup: A steady desk, palms flat on it, fingers pointing back at you.
596.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if a wrist or an elbow hurts.
tips: Lean back only as far as both palms stay flat.
Keep your elbows straight but soft, never pushed hard.
Lean a little further over the days, only as far as your wrists stay easy.

597.cue: Arms straight, shift your shoulders out over one hand. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand a step back and put your palms flat on the desk, a bit wider than your shoulders.
Turn your hands so your fingers point out to the sides.
Keep your arms straight and shift your shoulders sideways past one wrist.
Hold the lean with both palms flat and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
597.name: Side wrist lean at the desk
597.setup: A steady desk, palms flat on it, fingers turned out to the sides.
597.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if a wrist hurts.
tips: Press the heel of the hand you lean over into the desk.
Move your hips and shoulders together, as one.

598.cue: Press your fingertips down, palms up, lean in. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand a step back from the desk and spread your fingers on it, shoulder-width apart.
Press into your fingertips and thumbs until your palms lift off the desk.
Keep your arms straight and lean in until your shoulders are over your fingers.
Hold the tent shape with your fingers and breathe slowly.
Lower your palms and ease back at the end of the hold.
598.name: Fingertip lean at the desk
598.setup: A steady desk, fingertips and thumbs on it, palms lifted off.
598.stop: Ease off at once if a finger or a wrist hurts.
tips: Spread your fingers wide so all five share the weight.
If your palms sink, lean less and lift them again.

599.cue: Lean in, gently press your fingers down for 5 s, relax and lean on. Breathe out.
how: Set up as for the wrist lean: palms flat, fingers forward, arms straight.
Lean until your shoulders pass your wrists and you feel a pull in your forearms.
Gently press your fingers into the desk at about half effort for 5 s.
Relax, breathe out and lean a little further.
Do three rounds in the hold, breathing all the time.
599.name: Wrist lean, press and sink
599.setup: A steady desk, palms flat on it, fingers pointing away from you.
599.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if a wrist hurts.
tips: Press at half effort only: a gentle push, never a strain.
Keep breathing while you press, never hold your breath.
Keep both palms flat as you lean further.

60.cue: Pull it to your hip, lower it in 3 seconds. Count out loud, breathe out as you pull.
how: The one-arm row's weight: a bag of books or bottles, a full jug, a kettlebell or dumbbell.
Face the desk, free hand flat on it, step back on the weight's side, back flat.
Pull the weight to your hip in 1 s, then lower it for a full 3 s to a long arm.
Breathe out as you pull, breathe in slowly as you lower.
Count each rep out loud; every rep on one side, then press Switch sides and swap hands.

dumbbells: Face the desk, free hand flat on it, step back on the dumbbell's side, back flat.
Pull the dumbbell to your hip in 1 s, then lower it for a full 3 s to a long arm.
Breathe out as you pull, breathe in slowly as you lower.
Count each rep out loud; every rep on one side, then press Switch sides and swap hands.
kettlebell: Face the desk, free hand flat on it, step back on the kettlebell's side, back flat.
Pull the bell to your hip in 1 s, then lower it for a full 3 s to a long arm.
Breathe out as you pull, breathe in slowly as you lower.
Count each rep out loud; every rep on one side, then press Switch sides and swap hands.

60.name: One-arm row, slow lowering
60.setup: One hand on the desk, a weight of 5-15 kg in the other: a bag, a jug.

setups.dumbbells: One hand on the desk, a dumbbell of 5-15 kg in the other.
setups.kettlebell: One hand on the desk, a kettlebell of 5-15 kg in the other.

60.stop: Stop when you lose the 3-s lowering. Count the weaker side.
tips: Count the lowering in your head, one and two and three, so it never speeds up.
10 slow reps should be work and 20 hard: the game says when to go heavier.
Nothing near? Hold a light chair without wheels upright by the side of its seat.

600.cue: Body straight, push the desk away, lean your shoulders past your hands. Breathe slowly.
how: Put your hands flat on the desk, shoulder-width apart, fingers turned out a little.
Walk your feet back until your body is one straight line, up on your toes.
Push the desk away so your upper back rounds a little.
Lean forward until your shoulders are over your fingertips, arms straight.
Breathe slowly in the lean, then shift back over your feet.
600.name: Planche lean at the desk
600.setup: A steady desk, hands on it turned out a little, feet back on your toes.
600.stop: Ease off if a wrist or an elbow hurts or the desk moves.
tips: Keep your hips in line with your body, never sagging or piked.
Check that the desk stays put before you lean your weight on it.
Lean a little further over the days, only as far as your wrists stay easy.

601.cue: Lean, gently press your fingers down for 5 s, relax and lean on. Breathe out.
how: Put your hands flat on the desk, fingers turned out a little, body straight on your toes.
Lean your shoulders past your wrists until your forearms pull.
Gently press your fingers into the desk at about half effort for 5 s.
Relax, breathe out and lean a little further, arms straight.
Do three rounds in the hold, breathing all the time.
601.name: Planche lean at the desk, press and sink
601.setup: A steady desk, hands on it turned out a little, feet back on your toes.
601.stop: Ease off if a wrist or an elbow hurts or the desk moves.
tips: Press at half effort only: a gentle push, never a strain.
Keep your body one straight line from your heels to your head.
Keep breathing while you press, never hold your breath.

602.cue: Arms straight, lean your shoulders forward past your hands. Breathe slowly.
how: Kneel on all fours, hands under your shoulders, fingers spread and pointing forward.
Keep your arms straight and your back flat.
Lean forward until your shoulders pass over your fingertips.
Breathe slowly in the lean, then rock back over your knees.
602.name: Wrist lean on all fours
602.setup: Knees on a mat or a folded towel, palms flat, fingers forward.
602.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if a wrist hurts.
tips: Press the whole hand down, most of all the base of the first finger.
Lean a little further over the days, only as far as your wrists stay easy.

603.cue: Arms straight, sit back until your forearms stretch. Breathe slowly.
how: Kneel on all fours with your hands under your shoulders.
Turn your hands so your fingers point back at your knees, palms flat.
Keep your arms straight and sit your hips back toward your heels.
Stop when your shoulders are a fist behind your wrists, and breathe slowly.
Rock forward again at the end of the hold.
603.name: Reverse wrist lean on all fours
603.setup: Knees on a mat or a folded towel, palms flat, fingers pointing at your knees.
603.stop: Ease off at a strong pull or if a wrist or an elbow hurts.
tips: Sit back only as far as both palms stay flat.
Keep your elbows straight but soft, never pushed hard.

604.cue: Shins crossed, press the books away, lift your seat and knees. Breathe slowly.
how: Kneel and sit on your heels, then cross your shins, the tops of your feet on the floor.
Put your hands flat on the books beside your thighs.
Round your back and draw your knees toward your chest.
Press the books away and lift your seat and knees, the feet still down.
Breathe slowly in the lift, then lower slowly at the end of the hold.
604.name: Pendant prep on books
604.setup: Two stacks of books beside your knees, about 10 cm high, on a mat.
604.stop: Come down at once if a wrist or a knee hurts.
tips: Push down through your hands, never lean back onto your feet.
Draw your belly in to help your knees come up.

605.cue: Knees high on your arms, lift both feet, press your arms straight. Breathe slowly.
how: Start in the crow: knees high on your upper arms, both feet off the floor.
Press the floor away and slowly straighten your arms.
Lift your hips higher as your arms straighten, knees pressing into your arms.
Hold with your eyes ahead of your hands and breathe slowly.
Bend your arms and lower your feet slowly at the end of the hold.
605.name: Crane, straight arms
605.setup: A pillow on the floor in front of your hands in case you tip forward.
605.stop: Come down at once if a wrist or an elbow hurts.
tips: Squeeze your knees into your arms so they stay high.
Round your upper back as you press up.
Look forward at the floor, not down at your hands.

606.cue: Shins crossed, press the books away, lift your whole body. Breathe slowly.
how: Start in the pendant prep: shins crossed, hands on the books, seat and knees up.
Draw your heels toward your seat and round your back more.
Press the books away until your feet lift too.
Hold your whole body off the floor and breathe slowly.
Lower your feet and knees slowly at the end of the hold.
606.name: Pendant on books
606.setup: Two stacks of books beside your knees, about 10 cm high, a pillow in front.
606.stop: Come down at once if a wrist, an elbow or a knee hurts.
tips: Lift one foot first if both will not come up yet.
Draw your belly in and keep pressing down through your hands.

607.cue: Elbows into your belly, lean forward, lift your legs straight. Breathe slowly.
how: Kneel and put your hands flat on the floor, fingers pointing back at your knees.
Bend your elbows and set them into your belly, just below your ribs.
Stretch your legs back, toes down, so your body is one straight line.
Lean forward over your hands until your feet float and your body is level.
Breathe slowly in the hold, then lower your toes slowly.
607.name: Peacock
607.setup: A pillow on the floor in front of your face in case you tip forward.
607.stop: Come down at once if a wrist or an elbow hurts.
tips: Keep your hands close together so your elbows stay under your belly.
Lift one leg first if both will not come up yet.
Look forward at the floor with your chin level.

608.cue: Side crow, then stretch your top leg out straight to the side. Breathe slowly.
how: Start in the side crow: knees stacked on one upper arm, both feet up.
Keep the bottom knee on your arm and lean a little further forward.
Slowly straighten your top leg out to the side, level with your hip.
Hold with the leg straight and the foot flexed, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
608.name: Side crow, one leg straight
608.setup: A pillow on the floor in front of and beside your hands in case you tip.
608.stop: Come down at once if a wrist or an elbow hurts.
tips: Lean forward as the leg straightens so you stay balanced.
Bend the leg back in first if you start to tip.

609.cue: Shin across your arms, foot hooked, back foot on the books. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand on one leg and cross the other ankle over that knee, a figure four.
Fold forward and put your hands flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Set the crossed shin across both upper arms and hook its foot round the arm.
Bend your elbows, lean forward and rest the back foot on the books.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
609.name: Flying pigeon, back foot on books
609.setup: A stack of books 12 cm high behind you, a pillow in front of your hands.
609.stop: Come down at once if a wrist, a hip or a knee hurts.
tips: Keep the hooked foot flexed so it holds on to the arm.
Lean forward only as far as you can press back up.

61.cue: Lift your arms in a Y, a T, then a W, thumbs up. Breathe out as you lift.
how: Lie face down on the floor, legs long, forehead resting on a folded towel.
Reach your arms overhead in a Y, thumbs up, lift them off the floor, then lower.
Do the same with straight arms out to the sides in a T, then with bent elbows in a W.
Breathe out as you lift and breathe in as you lower.
One Y, one T and one W together make one rep.
61.name: Y-T-W raises
61.setup: Lie face down on the floor, forehead on a towel.
61.stop: Stop when your shoulders shrug or your lower back arches.
tips: Pull your shoulder blades down and together before your arms leave the floor.
Keep your forehead on the towel so your neck stays long the whole time.
In the W, draw your elbows down towards your ribs as you lift.

610.cue: Knees stacked on one arm, lift both feet, press your arms straight. Breathe slowly.
how: Start in the side crow: knees stacked on one upper arm, both feet in the air.
Press the floor away and slowly straighten your arms.
Keep your knees together and your feet level with your knees.
Hold with your eyes ahead of your hands and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
610.name: Side crane, straight arms
610.setup: A pillow on the floor in front of and beside your hands in case you tip.
610.stop: Come down at once if a wrist or an elbow hurts.
tips: Squeeze your knees together so they stay stacked.
Bend your elbows again before you lower your feet.

611.cue: Legs over your arms, press up, straighten your legs. Breathe slowly.
how: Squat, feet wide, shoulders behind your knees, hands flat behind your heels.
Sit your thighs high on your upper arms and lift your feet.
Press the floor away and straighten your arms as far as they go.
Slowly straighten your legs forward and up, and breathe slowly.
Bend your knees and lower your feet slowly at the end of the hold.
611.name: Firefly
611.setup: A pillow on the floor behind you in case you tip back.
611.stop: Come down at once if a wrist, an elbow or a hip hurts.
tips: Press the base of your first finger into the floor.
Reach out through your heels to keep your knees straight.

612.cue: Hip on one arm, legs out straight to the side, lean and lift. Breathe slowly.
how: Start in the side crow: knees stacked on one upper arm, both feet up.
Shift so the outer hip rests on that upper arm.
Lean forward and slowly straighten both legs out to the side.
Hold with your legs stacked, level with your hips, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
612.name: Side crow, straight legs
612.setup: A pillow on the floor in front of and beside your hands in case you tip.
612.stop: Come down at once if a wrist or an elbow hurts.
tips: Lean forward as your legs straighten so you stay balanced.
Keep your legs straight and stacked, feet flexed.

613.cue: Shin across your arms, lean forward, lift and straighten the back leg. Breathe slowly.
how: Start in the flying pigeon prep: shin hooked across both arms, back foot down.
Bend your elbows and lean forward until the back foot grows light.
Lift the back foot and straighten that leg behind you.
Hold with your hips level and your eyes ahead, and breathe slowly.
The clock times each side, then counts you in to switch.
613.name: Flying pigeon
613.setup: A pillow on the floor in front of your hands in case you tip forward.
613.stop: Come down at once if a wrist, a hip or a knee hurts.
tips: Keep the hooked foot flexed so it holds on to the arm.
Lift the back leg only as high as your hips stay level.

62.cue: Slide your arms up and down the wall like a snow angel. Breathe slowly.
how: Stand with your heels a foot's length from the wall, knees soft.
Press your bottom, upper back and the back of your head to the wall.
Arms in a W on the wall, slide them up until straight by your ears, then back down.
Breathe slowly as your arms slide up and back down.
Move at an easy pace for the time shown.
62.name: Wall angels
62.setup: Back, head and hips against the wall.
62.stop: Stop when your back leaves the wall.
tips: Keep your ribs down so your lower back stays close to the wall as your arms rise.
Slide only as high as your hands can stay within a fist of the wall.
Tuck your chin slightly so the back of your head stays on the wall.

620.cue: Step to the side and bring the other foot in, then back the other way. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Stand tall in the cleared space, feet together, knees soft, hands up in front of you.
Step one foot out to the side and bring the other foot in to meet it.
Step back the other way the same, to and fro across the space.
Swing your arms with the steps and keep the pace brisk.
Breathe in rhythm, fast enough that you cannot say a full sentence.
620.name: Side steps
620.setup: Clear a step's width to each side.
tips: Stay on the balls of your feet so the steps stay light and quiet.
Keep your knees soft and your chest up, and never cross your feet.

621.cue: March on the spot and punch straight out with each step. Breathe out on each punch.
how: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, fists by your chin, elbows in.
March on the spot, lifting each knee to hip height.
Punch straight out with the hand opposite the lifted knee, then bring it back.
Keep marching and punching in one steady rhythm, breathing out on each punch.
March fast enough that you cannot say a full sentence.
621.name: Punch march
621.setup: Clear arm's length in front of you.
621.stop: Stop if your elbows snap straight.
tips: Bring each fist back to your chin as fast as it went out.
Stop each punch just short of a straight elbow.

622.cue: Drive a knee up as your hands pull down; each strike counts one. Breathe out on each.
how: Stand in a boxing stance, one foot a short step ahead, fists up by your chin.
Reach both hands forward as if gripping a shoulder at chest height.
Drive one knee up hard as both hands pull down to meet it.
Put the foot back down and drive the other knee; each strike counts one.
Go as fast as clean strikes allow, breathing out on every strike.
622.name: Knee strikes
622.setup: Clear a small space, fists up by your chin.
622.stop: Slow down if you lose your balance.
tips: Rise onto the ball of the standing foot as the knee drives up.
Keep your chest up; bring the knee up rather than your chest down.

623.cue: Squat until your thighs are nearly level, stand fast; each counts one. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out a little, hands in front.
Sit your hips back and down until your thighs are nearly level.
Drive up fast through your whole foot and stand tall; each stand counts one.
Go straight into the next squat without a pause at the top.
Go as fast as clean reps allow, breathing hard and freely.
623.name: Speed squats
623.setup: Clear a small space, a floor that does not slip.
623.stop: Slow down when your knees cave in or your heels lift.
tips: Keep your knees in line with your toes all the way down and up.
Keep your heels on the floor and never bounce at the bottom.

624.cue: Jump the feet wide and back in, hips level; each jump in counts one. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Place your hands flat on the floor under your shoulders, fingers spread.
Step back into a high plank, body straight from heels to head, feet together.
Jump both feet out wide, then back together, like a jumping jack lying down.
Keep your hips level and your shoulders over your hands the whole time.
Go as fast as clean reps allow, breathing hard and freely.
624.name: Plank jacks
624.setup: Hands on the floor under your shoulders, a floor that does not slip.
624.stop: Stop when your hips sag or pike up.
tips: Land softly on the balls of your feet so the jumps stay light.
Brace your belly so your hips do not bounce with your feet.

625.cue: Each knee driven across to the other elbow counts one. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Place your hands flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart, fingers spread wide.
Step back into a high plank, body straight from heels to head.
Drive one knee across your body toward the other elbow, then step it back.
Switch legs fast; each knee across counts one, so a left and a right make two.
Go as fast as clean reps allow, breathing hard and freely.
625.name: Cross climbers
625.setup: Hands on the floor under your shoulders.
625.stop: Stop when your hips pike up.
tips: Keep your shoulders over your hands as the knees cross.
Let your hips turn a little with each knee, then square them again.

626.cue: Lunge back, then drive that knee up as you stand; each counts one. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, hands up in front of your chest.
Step one foot back into a lunge until the back knee is just above the floor.
Drive up off the front foot and swing the back knee up to hip height.
Put it down beside the other foot, then lunge back with the other leg.
Go as fast as clean reps allow; each knee drive counts one.
626.name: Lunge knee drives
626.setup: Clear a step behind you, a floor that does not slip.
626.stop: Slow down when your front knee caves in.
tips: Keep your front knee over your foot as you go down and up.
Stand tall on the front leg at the top before the next lunge.

627.cue: Step back, chest to the floor, push up, step in, stand and reach. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Stand with a body length of clear floor behind you, feet hip-width apart.
Squat, put your hands flat on the floor and step your feet back one at a time.
Lower your chest to the floor, then push up to the straight line again.
Step your feet back in one at a time, stand tall and reach both arms overhead.
Go as fast as clean reps allow, breathing hard and freely all the way through.
627.name: Step-back burpee
627.setup: A body length of clear floor behind you.
tips: Count a rep only when the chest touched the floor and the arms reached up.
Step, never jump, so it stays quiet.

628.cue: Jump from a lunge and switch legs in the air; each landing counts one. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Step into a lunge, front knee over your foot, back knee just above the floor.
Swing your arms and jump straight up out of the lunge.
Switch your legs in the air and land softly in a lunge on the other side.
Sink straight into the next jump; each landing counts one.
Go as fast as clean reps allow, breathing hard and freely.
628.name: Jump lunges
628.setup: Clear space, shoes on, a floor that does not slip.
628.stop: Stop when your landings get loud or your front knee caves in.
tips: Land on the whole front foot with a soft knee, never with a straight leg.
Keep your chest up and jump straight up, not forward.

629.cue: Sprawl, jump in, stand, then a jab and a cross; each round counts one. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Stand with a body length of clear floor behind you, fists up by your chin.
Drop your hands to the floor and shoot your legs back, hips down to the floor.
Jump your feet back in to your hands and stand up, fists back to your chin.
Punch a straight jab, then a cross, fists back to your chin; the round counts one.
Go as fast as clean rounds allow, breathing hard and freely.
629.name: Sprawl and strike
629.setup: A body length of clear floor behind you, shoes on.
tips: Drop your hips low on the sprawl so your back stays flat.
Turn your back hip into the cross, breathing out on each punch.

630.cue: Lunge back each side, a jab and a cross at the bottom; both count one. Breathe out.
how: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, fists up by your chin.
Step one foot back into a lunge until the back knee is just above the floor.
At the bottom, punch a straight jab, then a cross, fists back to your chin.
Stand up, then lunge back with the other foot and punch again; both sides count one.
Go as fast as clean reps allow, breathing out on each punch.
630.name: Lunge and strike
630.setup: Clear a step behind you and arm's length in front.
630.stop: Slow down when your front knee caves in.
tips: Keep your front knee over your foot and your chest up as you punch.
Stop each punch just short of a straight elbow.

631.cue: Step back, chest down and push up twice, step in, stand and reach. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Stand with a body length of clear floor behind you, feet hip-width apart.
Squat, put your hands flat on the floor and step your feet back one at a time.
Lower your chest to the floor and push up, then do it once more.
Step your feet back in one at a time, stand tall and reach both arms overhead.
Go as fast as clean reps allow, breathing hard and freely all the way through.
631.name: Stepped chest burpee
631.setup: A body length of clear floor behind you.
tips: Count a rep only when the chest touched the floor twice and the arms reached up.
Step, never jump, so it stays quiet.

632.cue: Step back, chest to the edge, push up, step in, stand and reach. Breathe out as you stand.
how: Stand facing the desk, a step back from its edge.
Put your hands on the desk edge and step one foot back, then the other, into a plank.
Lower your chest to the desk edge, then push back up to straight arms.
Step the feet back in one at a time, then stand tall and reach both arms overhead.
Keep a hard pace where you can say only a word or two.
632.name: Desk push-up burpee
632.setup: Hands on a sturdy desk edge, room behind you to step back.
tips: Keep your body straight from heels to head as your chest goes down.
Lock your hands on the edge before each step back.
Step, never jump, so it stays quiet.

633.cue: Step back, step in, stand, then drive a knee up each side. Breathe out on every knee.
how: Stand facing the desk, a step back from its edge.
Put your hands on the desk edge and step one foot back, then the other, into a plank.
Step the feet back in one at a time and stand tall.
Drive one knee up to hip height, then the other, and reach both arms overhead.
Keep a hard pace where you can say only a word or two.
633.name: Desk burpee with knees
633.setup: Hands on a sturdy desk edge, room behind you to step back.
tips: Pull your hands down to meet each knee as if gripping a shoulder.
Lock your hands on the edge before each step back.

634.cue: From a half squat, jump up with arms and legs wide, land softly. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Stand with feet hip-width apart in the cleared space, arms by your sides.
Sink into a half squat with your hands low in front of your knees.
Jump straight up and spread your arms and legs wide like a star.
Bring them back in and land softly in the half squat; each jump counts one.
Go as fast as clean reps allow, breathing hard and freely.
634.name: Star jumps
634.setup: Clear space, shoes on, a floor that does not slip.
634.stop: Stop when your landings get loud or your knees cave in.
tips: Land on the balls of your feet with soft knees, then let your heels come down.
Keep your knees in line with your toes as you land.

635.cue: Step back, push up twice, a spider step each side, step in, stand. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Stand with a body length of clear floor behind you, feet hip-width apart.
Squat, put your hands flat on the floor and step your feet back one at a time.
Lower your chest to the floor and push up, then do it once more.
Step one foot up outside its hand and back, then the other foot.
Step your feet back in, stand tall and reach both arms overhead.
635.name: Stepped spider burpee
635.setup: A body length of clear floor behind you.
tips: Count a rep only when both push-ups and both spider steps were done.
Keep your hips low as each foot steps up beside its hand.
Step, never jump, so it stays quiet.

636.cue: Step back, push up, each knee out to its elbow, step in, stand. Breathe out as you stand.
how: Stand facing the desk, a step back from its edge.
Put your hands on the desk edge and step one foot back, then the other, into a plank.
Lower your chest to the desk edge, then push back up to straight arms.
Bring one knee out to its elbow and back, then the other knee.
Step the feet back in, stand tall and reach both arms overhead.
636.name: Desk spider burpee
636.setup: Hands on a sturdy desk edge, room behind you to step back.
tips: Keep your hips level as each knee comes out to the side.
Lock your hands on the edge before each step back.

637.cue: Step back, step in, stand, jab, cross, a knee up each side. Breathe out on each strike.
how: Stand facing the desk, a step back from its edge.
Put your hands on the desk edge and step one foot back, then the other, into a plank.
Step the feet back in one at a time and stand up, fists by your chin.
Punch a jab and a cross, then drive one knee up and then the other.
Keep a hard pace where you can say only a word or two.
637.name: Desk burpee combo
637.setup: Hands on a sturdy desk edge, room behind you to step back.
tips: Bring each fist back to your chin before the next strike.
Lock your hands on the edge before each step back.

638.cue: Jump, pull your knees up to your chest, land softly and go again. Breathe in rhythm.
how: Stand with feet hip-width apart in the cleared space, knees soft.
Dip and swing your arms, then jump straight up.
Pull both knees up toward your chest at the top of the jump.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and go straight into the next jump.
Go as fast as clean reps allow, breathing hard and freely; each jump counts one.
638.name: Tuck jump rally
638.setup: Clear space, shoes on, a floor that does not slip.
638.stop: Stop when your landings get loud or your knees cave in.
tips: Bring your knees up to your chest; do not fold your chest down to them.
Land with soft knees in line with your toes, then let your heels come down.

639.cue: Hips back, back flat at a slant, arms reaching forward. Count out loud.
how: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, arms by your sides.
Push your hips back and tip your chest forward with your back flat.
Stop when your chest is about halfway to level and reach your arms forward.
Hold still with your back flat, breathing slowly and counting out loud.
The clock times how long your back stays flat, then stand back up.
639.name: Hinge hold
639.setup: Feet hip-width apart, knees soft, nothing in your hands.
639.stop: Stop when your back rounds or your lower back aches.
tips: Keep your neck long, your eyes on the floor a step in front of you.
Squeeze your seat and feel the muscles beside your spine working.

64.cue: Hang with straight arms, shoulders gently engaged. Count out loud.
how: Check the bar is fixed firmly and set the stool under it to step up and down.
Grip the bar with palms facing away, hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Lift your feet and hang with straight arms, knees slightly bent, feet together.
Draw your shoulders a little away from your ears and breathe slowly throughout.
Count out loud while the clock times the hang, from the moment your feet leave the stool.
64.name: Dead hang
64.setup: A bar fixed firmly; a stool to step down on.
64.stop: Stop when your grip starts to slip.
tips: Wrap your thumbs around the bar and squeeze it with your whole hand.
Keep your ribs down and your legs still so your body hangs without swinging.
Relax your neck and look straight ahead, not up at the bar.

640.cue: Lift your arms, chest and legs a little off the floor. Count out loud.
how: Lie face down on a mat, arms straight out past your head, legs straight.
Squeeze your seat and lift your arms, chest and legs a hand's width off the floor.
Keep your neck long, your eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands.
Hold still and breathe slowly, counting out loud.
The clock times how long you hold the lift, then lower everything slowly.
640.name: Superman hold
640.setup: Lie face down on the floor, arms reaching past your head.
640.stop: Stop when your lower back aches or your legs drop.
tips: Lift with your seat and back, never by throwing your head back.
Reach long through your fingers and toes rather than high.

641.cue: Reach one arm and the other leg level with your back and hold. Count out loud.
how: Kneel on the floor, hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips, back flat.
Reach one arm forward and the other leg back until both are level with your back.
Hold still with your hips level, breathing slowly and counting out loud.
When this side ends, press Switch sides and reach the other arm and leg.
641.name: Bird dog hold
641.setup: Hands and knees on the floor, a folded towel under your knees if it is hard.
641.stop: Stop when your hips rotate or your back sags. Count the weaker side.
tips: Push the heel back as if pressing a wall behind you, not up to the ceiling.
Keep both hip bones pointing at the floor the whole hold.

642.cue: Thighs level, one foot a half step ahead with most of your weight on it. Count out loud.
how: Stand with your back to the wall, heels about 60 cm out, feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot a half step forward and put most of your weight on it.
Slide down until your thighs are level, the front knee over its ankle.
Hold still and breathe slowly, counting out loud.
When this side ends, stand, press Switch sides and put the other foot ahead.
642.name: Staggered wall sit
642.setup: Back flat on the wall, nothing slippery under your feet.
642.stop: Stop when you slide or your knee aches. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep the back foot light, resting on the floor for balance only.
Keep the front knee over its ankle, never past your toes.

643.cue: Thighs level, punch straight ahead, one fist then the other. Count out loud.
how: Stand with your back to the wall, feet hip-width apart and heels about 60 cm out.
Slide down until your thighs are level with the floor, knees right over your ankles.
Punch one fist straight ahead and back to your chin, then the other.
Keep punching at an easy pace, breathing out on each punch and counting out loud.
The clock times how long you hold your thighs level, then slide back up to stand.
643.name: Wall sit punches
643.setup: Back flat on the wall, nothing slippery under your feet.
643.stop: Stop when you slide or your knees ache.
tips: Keep your shoulders and lower back on the wall as your arms punch.
Stop each punch just short of a straight elbow.

644.cue: Push the seat away, hips off its edge, knees tucked, feet off. Count out loud.
how: Set a stable chair against a wall and sit on its front edge, feet flat.
Put your hands on the front corners of the seat beside your hips and lock your arms.
Push the seat away, slide your hips just off its edge and lift both feet.
Pull your knees up toward your chest and hold, breathing slowly.
The clock counts up: hold until a foot lands or your shoulders rise.
644.name: Chair tuck hold
644.setup: A stable chair that cannot tip; hands on the front corners of its seat.
644.stop: Stop when a foot touches down or your shoulders creep up.
tips: Push your shoulders down away from your ears the whole hold.
Keep your chest up; do not let it cave in over your knees.

645.cue: Hips off the edge, one leg straight out, the other knee tucked. Count out loud.
how: Set a stable chair against a wall and sit on its front edge, feet flat.
Put your hands on the front corners of the seat beside your hips and lock your arms.
Push the seat away, slide your hips just off its edge and tuck both knees up.
Straighten one leg out level with your hips and hold, counting out loud.
When this side ends, press Switch sides and straighten the other leg.
645.name: Chair one-leg hold
645.setup: A stable chair that cannot tip; hands on the front corners of its seat.
645.stop: Stop when the straight leg drops or your shoulders creep up. Count the weaker side.
tips: Push your shoulders down away from your ears the whole hold.
Lock the straight knee and point your toes.

646.cue: Hips off the edge, both legs straight out level with your hips. Count out loud.
how: Set a stable chair against a wall and sit on its front edge, feet flat.
Put your hands on the front corners of the seat beside your hips and lock your arms.
Push the seat away and slide your hips just off its edge.
Lift both legs straight out level with your hips and hold, breathing slowly.
The clock counts up: hold until your heels drop or your knees bend.
646.name: Chair L-sit
646.setup: A stable chair that cannot tip; hands on the front corners of its seat.
646.stop: Stop when your knees bend or your shoulders creep up.
tips: Push your shoulders down away from your ears the whole hold.
Lock both knees and squeeze your thighs together.

647.cue: Arms straight, squeeze your shoulder blades back, release. Breathe out as you squeeze.
how: Face the edge of a solid doorframe and grip it at chest height, one hand above the other.
Toes near the frame, lean back until your arms are straight, heels to head in one line.
Keeping the arms straight, pull your shoulder blades back and down, lifting your chest.
Breathe out as you squeeze, hold a beat, then let your shoulders slide forward again.
Each squeeze counts as one rep.
647.name: Doorframe shoulder-blade pull
647.setup: Grip a solid doorframe at chest height, feet close to it.
647.stop: Stop when your elbows bend or your shoulders shrug.
tips: Think of putting your shoulder blades in your back pockets.
Never bend the elbows: the move is all in the shoulder blades.
Grip only where your whole hand closes around the frame, never trim with fingertips.

648.cue: Pull your chest to the frame on one arm. Count out loud, breathe out as you pull.
how: Face the frame's edge on the side without hinges and wrap one hand around it.
Set your toes one foot's length from the base and lean back until the arm is straight.
Pull your chest to the frame, elbow close to your side, then lower slowly.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lean back.
Each pull counts as one rep; do one side, press Switch sides, then the other.
648.name: One-arm doorframe row, feet back
648.setup: One hand on a solid doorframe edge at chest height, toes a foot's length from its base.
648.stop: Stop when your hand slips or your hips twist. Count the weaker side.
tips: Measure the gap once with your own foot and stand there every time.
Keep the free hand hovering by the frame, ready to catch you.
Grip only where your whole hand closes around the frame, never trim with fingertips.

649.cue: Pull to the frame on one arm and hold, elbow back. Count out loud, keep breathing.
how: Face the frame's edge on the side without hinges and wrap one hand around it.
Set your toes a hand's length from the base and lean back until the arm is straight.
Pull your chest to the frame and hold there, elbow back and shoulder down.
Keep breathing slowly and count out loud through the whole hold.
The clock counts up: hold until your chest sinks, then press Switch sides.
649.name: One-arm doorframe row hold
649.setup: One hand on a solid doorframe edge at chest height, toes a hand's length from its base.
649.stop: Stop when your hand slips or your chest caves in. Count the weaker side.
tips: Keep the free hand hovering by the frame, ready to catch you.
Draw the shoulder blade back and down and keep it there the whole hold.
Grip only where your whole hand closes around the frame, never trim with fingertips.

65.cue: Hang, then pull your shoulder blades down without bending your arms. Count out loud.
how: Check the bar is fixed firmly and set the stool under it to step down on.
Grip with palms facing away, hands a little wider than your shoulders, and hang.
With straight arms, pull your shoulder blades down so your body rises a little.
Pull down, pause, then let your shoulders rise back slowly.
Breathe out as you pull down and count each rep out loud.
65.name: Scapular pulls
65.setup: A bar fixed firmly; a stool to step down on.
tips: Think of putting your shoulder blades into your back pockets.
Keep your elbows locked so the whole lift comes from your shoulders.
Let your chest lift slightly towards the bar at the top of each pull.

650.cue: Heels up, body flat, pull your chest to the edge. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Lean on the edge, then pull gently: if the table lifts, slides or creaks, stop.
Set a sofa, a bed or a chair without wheels in line with the table, your height away.
Lie under the table, grip the edge a little wider than your shoulders, heels on the seat.
Lift your hips so your body is flat, then pull your chest to the edge.
Lower until your arms are straight, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.
650.name: Table row, feet up
650.setup: A heavy table on four legs; heels up on a sofa, a bed or a chair without wheels.
650.stop: Stop when your hips sag or the table moves.
tips: Squeeze your bottom and belly so your hips rise with your chest, not after it.
Drive your elbows down towards the floor and squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Higher heels make it harder: use the same seat each time so your record stays fair.

651.cue: Pack on your chest, body flat, pull to the edge. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Lean on the edge, then pull gently: if the table lifts, slides or creaks, stop.
Load a backpack with books or bottles and wear it back to front, on your chest.
Lie under the table, grip the edge, and rest your heels on the sofa, bed or chair.
Lift your hips so your body is flat, then pull your chest to the edge.
Lower until your arms are straight, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.

vest: Lean on the edge, then pull gently: if the table lifts, slides or creaks, stop.
Put on the weighted vest, snug and even.
Lie under the table, grip the edge, and rest your heels on the sofa, bed or chair.
Lift your hips so your body is flat, then pull your chest to the edge.
Lower until your arms are straight, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.

651.name: Table row, feet up, with a backpack
651.setup: A heavy table on four legs; a backpack of 5-15 kg worn on your chest, heels up.

setups.vest: A heavy table on four legs; a weighted vest of 5-15 kg, heels up on a sofa or bed.

651.stop: Stop when your hips sag or the table moves.
tips: Pick a load where 3 reps are work and 12 hard: the game says when to go heavier.
1 L of water weighs 1 kg, a hardback about 1 kg: most people start at 5 kg.
Squeeze your bottom and belly so your hips rise with your chest, not after it.

652.cue: Pull your chest to the edge, hold 2 seconds, lower. Count out loud, breathe steadily.
how: Lean on the edge, then pull gently: if the table lifts, slides or creaks, stop.
Wear the loaded pack on your chest, straps tight, heels up on the sofa, bed or chair.
Lie under the table, grip the edge, and lift your hips so your body is flat.
Pull your chest to the edge, breathing out, and hold it there for 2 s.
Lower until your arms are straight, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.

vest: Lean on the edge, then pull gently: if the table lifts, slides or creaks, stop.
Put on the weighted vest, snug and even, heels up on the sofa, bed or chair.
Lie under the table, grip the edge, and lift your hips so your body is flat.
Pull your chest to the edge, breathing out, and hold it there for 2 s.
Lower until your arms are straight, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.

652.name: Paused table row, feet up
652.setup: A heavy table on four legs; a backpack of 5-15 kg worn on your chest, heels up.

setups.vest: A heavy table on four legs; a weighted vest of 5-15 kg, heels up on a sofa or bed.

652.stop: Stop when your hips sag, the table moves or you lose the 2-s hold.
tips: Say the two beats out loud at the top, which keeps you breathing.
At the top squeeze your shoulder blades and keep your elbows close to your ribs.
Keep the same load and seat each time: the game says when to go heavier.

653.cue: Heels up, body flat, pull your chest to your hands. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Shut and lock any door the straps hang from, then tug both handles hard to test them.
Hang the rings low, so your back just clears the floor when your arms are straight.
Lie under the rings, grip them, and rest your heels on a sofa, a bed or a chair.
Lift your hips so your body is flat, then pull your chest to your hands.
Lower until your arms are straight, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.
653.name: Ring row, feet up
653.setup: Rings or straps hung low; heels up on a sofa, a bed or a chair without wheels.
tips: Squeeze your bottom and belly so your hips rise with your chest, not after it.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top and let your palms face each other.
Higher heels make it harder: use the same seat each time so your record stays fair.

654.cue: Pack on your chest, body flat, pull to your hands. Count out loud, breathe out up.
how: Shut and lock any door the straps hang from, then tug both handles hard to test them.
Load a backpack with books or bottles and wear it back to front, on your chest.
Lie under the rings, grip them, and rest your heels on the sofa, bed or chair.
Lift your hips so your body is flat, then pull your chest to your hands.
Lower until your arms are straight, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.

vest: Shut and lock any door the straps hang from, then tug both handles hard to test them.
Put on the weighted vest, snug and even.
Lie under the rings, grip them, and rest your heels on the sofa, bed or chair.
Lift your hips so your body is flat, then pull your chest to your hands.
Lower until your arms are straight, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.

654.name: Ring row, feet up, with a backpack
654.setup: Rings or straps hung low; a backpack of 5-15 kg worn on your chest, heels up.

setups.vest: Rings or straps hung low; a weighted vest of 5-15 kg, heels up on a sofa or bed.

tips: Pick a load where 3 reps are work and 12 hard: the game says when to go heavier.
1 L of water weighs 1 kg, a hardback about 1 kg: most people start at 5 kg.
Squeeze your bottom and belly so your hips rise with your chest, not after it.

655.cue: Pull your chest to your hands, hold 2 seconds, lower. Count out loud, breathe steadily.
how: Shut and lock any door the straps hang from, then tug both handles hard to test them.
Wear the loaded pack on your chest, pulled snug, heels up on the sofa, bed or chair.
Lie under the rings, grip them, and lift your hips so your body is flat.
Pull your chest to your hands, breathing out, and hold it there for 2 s.
Lower until your arms are straight, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.

vest: Shut and lock any door the straps hang from, then tug both handles hard to test them.
Put on the weighted vest, snug and even, heels up on the sofa, bed or chair.
Lie under the rings, grip them, and lift your hips so your body is flat.
Pull your chest to your hands, breathing out, and hold it there for 2 s.
Lower until your arms are straight, then pull again. Count each rep out loud.

655.name: Paused ring row, feet up
655.setup: Rings or straps hung low; a backpack of 5-15 kg worn on your chest, heels up.

setups.vest: Rings or straps hung low; a weighted vest of 5-15 kg, heels up on a sofa or bed.

655.stop: Stop when your hips sag or you lose the 2-s hold.
tips: Say the two beats out loud at the top, which keeps you breathing.
At the top squeeze your shoulder blades and keep your elbows close to your ribs.
Keep the same load and seat each time: the game says when to go heavier.

66.cue: Start at the top, lower yourself as slowly as you can. Count out loud.
how: Check the bar is fixed firmly and set a stool under it, high enough to get your chin over.
Grip with palms facing away, step up and bring your chin over the bar, elbows tight.
Lift your feet and lower yourself as slowly as you can to straight arms.
Step back onto the stool to reset at the top, then lower again.
Breathe out slowly on the way down and count each lowering out loud as one rep.
66.name: Pull-up negative
66.setup: A bar fixed firmly; a stool to step up on.
tips: Keep the speed even all the way down, no faster near the bottom.
Squeeze your legs together and brace your belly so you do not swing.
Keep your shoulders down and back as you lower, away from your ears.

67.cue: Pull your chin over the bar, lower with control. Count out loud, breathe out as you pull.
how: Check the bar is firm, then hang a band from it or set a chair without wheels below.
Grip with palms away, hands a bit wider than your shoulders, one foot on the seat or band.
Start with straight arms, pull your chin over the bar, then lower slowly.
Push with your foot only as much as you need to reach the top.
Breathe out as you pull and count each rep out loud at the top.
67.name: Assisted pull-up
67.setup: A bar fixed firmly; a band or one foot on a chair without wheels.
67.stop: Stop when you kick or cannot reach the top.
tips: Pull your elbows down towards your ribs as if bending the bar.
Lower all the way to straight arms before the next pull.
Keep your chest up and aim it at the bar as you pull.

68.cue: From a dead hang, chin over the bar, lower fully. Count out loud, breathe out as you pull.
how: Check the bar is fixed firmly and set a stool under it to step down on.
Grip with palms facing away, hands a little wider than your shoulders.
From straight arms, pull your chin over the bar.
Lower all the way to straight arms, breathing in as you go down.
Breathe out as you pull and count each rep out loud at the top.
68.name: Pull-up
68.setup: A bar fixed firmly; a stool to step down on.
68.stop: Stop when you kick or cannot reach the top.
tips: Start each rep by pulling your shoulders down, then drive your elbows to your ribs.
Keep your legs together and a little forward so your body does not swing.
Aim your chest at the bar rather than stretching your chin up.

69.cue: Hang, knees to your chest, lower slowly. Count out loud, breathe out as you lift.
how: Check the bar is fixed firmly and set a stool under it to step down on.
Grip with palms facing away and hang with straight arms, shoulders gently engaged.
Lift your knees up towards your chest, tilting your hips up at the top.
Lower your legs slowly until they hang straight and still.
Breathe out as you lift and count each rep out loud.
69.name: Hanging knee raise
69.setup: A bar fixed firmly; a stool to step down on.
tips: Curl your hips up at the top so your belly does the lift, not a swing.
Start each lift from a still hang, never from the swing of the last one.
Squeeze the bar hard and keep your shoulders away from your ears.

7.cue: Stand up without your hands, rise onto your toes. Breathe out as you stand.
how: Sit near the edge of the bed or sofa, feet flat and a little behind your knees.
Sit tall with both arms reaching forward at shoulder height, hands off your legs.
Lean your chest forward over your feet, then press the floor away and stand up tall.
Rise onto your toes, lower your heels, then sit back down slowly with the same lean.
Breathe out as you stand and count one rep each time you are back on the edge.
7.name: Sit to stand with a calf raise
7.setup: Sit on the edge of a firm bed or sofa, feet flat and hip-width apart.
7.stop: Stop when you need your hands or your knees cave in.
tips: Go straight up onto your toes with your weight over the big toes, not rolling outwards.
Push through your whole foot so your knees stay in line with your toes as you rise.
Touch down on the edge lightly on the way back, never drop into it.

70.cue: Body straight from heels to head, belly tight. Count out loud.
how: Push on the desk first to check it stays put, then rest your forearms on its edge.
Put your elbows right under your shoulders, forearms parallel and pointing forward.
Walk your feet back onto your toes until your body is straight from heels to head.
Pull your belly in, squeeze your bottom and breathe slowly and steadily.
Count out loud while the clock times the hold, from the moment your body is straight.
70.name: Incline plank
70.setup: Forearms on the desk edge; the desk must not move.
70.stop: Stop when your hips sag or pike up.
tips: Press your forearms into the desk so your upper back stays wide, not sunk.
Tilt your hips as if tucking your tail, which keeps your lower back from arching.
Look down at the desk, not ahead, so your neck stays in line.

71.cue: Straight line from knees to head, belly tight. Count out loud.
how: Kneel on the floor, forearms down, elbows right under your shoulders.
Walk your knees back until your body is straight from knees to head.
Lower your hips into that line, belly pulled in, bottom gently squeezed.
Breathe slowly and steadily the whole time.
Count out loud while the clock times the hold, from the moment the line is straight.
71.name: Knee plank
71.setup: Forearms and knees on the floor, a folded towel under your knees if it is hard.
71.stop: Stop when your hips sag or pike up.
tips: Press the floor away with your forearms so your shoulders do not sink.
Tuck your tail slightly to keep your lower back from arching.
Look at the floor just ahead of your hands to keep your neck long.

72.cue: Body straight from heels to head, belly tight. Count out loud.
how: Lie face down on the floor, forearms down, elbows right under your shoulders.
Tuck your toes, feet hip-width apart, and lift your body off the floor.
Hold a straight line from heels to head, belly pulled in, bottom squeezed.
Breathe slowly and steadily through the whole hold.
Count out loud while the clock times the hold, from the moment you lift.
72.name: Forearm plank
72.setup: Forearms and toes on the floor.
72.stop: Stop when your hips sag or pike up.
tips: Drag your elbows towards your toes without moving them to switch your belly on.
Push your heels back as if pressing a wall behind you, legs tight.
Keep your gaze on the floor between your hands so your neck stays long.

73.cue: Hips up in a straight line from knees to head. Count out loud.
how: Lie on your side on the floor, elbow right under your shoulder, forearm pointing forward.
Bend your knees so your feet are behind you, hips and shoulders stacked.
Lift your hips until your body is straight from knees to head, top hand on your hip.
Breathe slowly and steadily through the whole hold.
Count out loud; when this side ends, press Switch sides, then turn over.
73.name: Side plank on the knees
73.setup: Forearm and knees on the floor, a folded towel under your knees if it is hard.
73.stop: Stop when your hips drop. Count the weaker side.
tips: Push the floor away with your forearm so your shoulder does not sink.
Press your hips forward a little so they stay in line and do not drift back.
Keep your head in line with your spine, eyes looking straight ahead.

74.cue: Hips up in a straight line from feet to head. Count out loud.
how: Lie on your side on the floor, elbow right under your shoulder, forearm pointing forward.
Stack your feet with your legs straight, hips and shoulders one above the other.
Lift your hips until your body is straight from feet to head, top hand on your hip.
Breathe slowly and steadily through the whole hold.
Count out loud; when this side ends, press Switch sides, then turn over.
74.name: Side plank
74.setup: Forearm and feet on the floor.
74.stop: Stop when your hips drop. Count the weaker side.
tips: Push the floor away with your forearm so your shoulder stays high.
Lift your lower hip a touch higher than feels natural, since it tends to sit low.
Squeeze your bottom and keep your top hip over the lower one, not rolled forward.

75.cue: Elbows ahead of your shoulders, tuck your tailbone, squeeze everything. Count out loud.
how: Kneel and put your forearms down, elbows a hand's width ahead of your shoulders.
Tuck your toes, feet close together, and lift into a straight line from heels to head.
Tuck your tailbone under and squeeze your bottom, thighs and fists hard.
Keep breathing in short, steady breaths while you squeeze.
Count out loud while the clock times the hold, from the moment you lift.
75.name: Long-lever plank
75.setup: Forearms and toes on the floor.
75.stop: Stop when your lower back sags.
tips: Make fists and press the outer edge of your forearms into the floor.
Pull your ribs down towards your hips so your lower back stays flat.
Look at the floor just ahead of your hands to keep your neck long.

76.cue: Tap each shoulder in turn, hips still. Count out loud.
how: Put your hands on the floor right under your shoulders, arms straight, fingers spread.
Tuck your toes, feet together, body straight from heels to head.
Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder, put it back, then tap with the other.
Keep a steady rhythm of about one tap a second and breathe freely.
Count out loud while the clock times the taps, from your first tap.
76.name: Plank shoulder taps
76.setup: Hands and toes on the floor, feet together.
76.stop: Stop when your hips rock or sag.
tips: Push the floor away hard with the standing hand as the other one lifts.
Squeeze your bottom and belly before each tap so your hips stay level.
Imagine a glass of water on your lower back and tap without spilling it.

77.cue: From a plank, slide forward and back from the shoulders. Count out loud.
how: Put a towel on a smooth floor, your forearms down ahead of it and your toes on the towel.
Lift into a straight line from heels to head, elbows under your shoulders.
Push from your shoulders to slide your body back a hand's length, then pull it forward.
Slide at an even pace and breathe steadily as you go.
Count out loud while the clock times the sawing, from your first slide.
77.name: Body saw
77.setup: Forearms down, toes on a towel on a smooth floor.
77.stop: Stop when your lower back sags.
tips: Move only at the shoulders, your hips and back stay in one straight line.
Pull your belly in hardest when your elbows are furthest ahead of your head.
Keep both feet together on the towel so it glides as one piece.

78.cue: Reach one arm and the opposite leg, hips level, alternate sides. Breathe out as you reach.
how: Kneel on the floor, hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips, back flat.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your back.
Hold the reach for 1 s with your hips level, then come back.
Breathe out as you reach, breathe in as you come back.
Alternate sides every rep; a reach with one side and then the other counts one.
78.name: Bird dog
78.setup: Hands and knees on the floor, a folded towel under your knees if it is hard.
78.stop: Stop when your hips rotate or your back sags. A reach on each side counts one.
tips: Push the heel back as if pressing a wall behind you, not up to the ceiling.
Keep both hip bones pointing at the floor as the leg reaches back.
Press the floor away with your standing hand so your upper back does not sag.

79.cue: Lower one arm and the opposite leg, lower back pressed down. Breathe out as you lower.
how: Lie on your back on the floor, arms straight up above your shoulders.
Lift your knees over your hips, bent to a right angle, lower back pressed down.
Lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg out straight, both just above the floor.
Bring them back to the start, breathing out as you lower and in as you return.
Switch sides every time and count each lower as one rep.
79.name: Dead bug
79.setup: Lie on your back on the floor, knees and arms up.
79.stop: Stop when your lower back lifts off the floor. Alternate sides; each lower counts one.
tips: Breathe out fully before you lower so your ribs sink and your back stays down.
Keep the other arm and leg still, only the working pair moves.
Reach long through the heel of the moving leg, toes pulled towards you.

8.cue: Bend a quarter of the way down, stand tall. Breathe out as you stand.
how: Stand facing the desk a small step back, feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Rest both hands on the desk edge and stand tall with your weight over the whole foot.
Push your hips back and bend your knees a quarter of the way down.
Breathe out and stand tall again, squeezing your seat.
Count one rep each time you are back up straight.
8.name: Quarter squat at the desk
8.setup: Hold the desk edge lightly; the desk must not move.
8.stop: Stop when your knees cave in or you lean on the desk.
tips: Keep only your fingertips on the desk so your legs do all the lifting.
Point your knees the same way as your toes, both on the way down and on the way up.
Keep your chest up and your eyes ahead so the bend comes from your hips and knees.

80.cue: Lift head and shoulders a little, hold 5 seconds, lower. Breathe out as you lift.
how: Lie on your back, one knee bent with the foot flat, the other leg long on the floor.
Slide your hands palms down under the small of your back to keep its natural curve.
Lift your head and shoulders a little off the floor as one piece, chin level, hold 5 s.
Breathe out as you lift, keep breathing gently through the hold, then lower.
Each lift and hold counts as one rep.
80.name: McGill curl-up
80.setup: Lie on the floor, one knee bent, hands under your lower back.
80.stop: Stop when your neck strains or your lower back flattens.
tips: Think of your head and chest as one stiff block, with no nodding at the neck.
Lift only a few centimetres, since the work is in keeping your belly tight.
Brace your belly as if someone were about to poke it before you lift.

81.cue: Lift your knees a hand's width off the floor, back flat. Count out loud.
how: Kneel on the floor, hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips, toes tucked.
Flatten your back so it is level from hips to head, eyes on the floor.
Lift your knees a hand's width off the floor and keep them there.
Breathe slowly and steadily through the whole hold.
Count out loud while the clock times the hold, from the moment your knees lift.
81.name: Bear plank
81.setup: Hands and knees on the floor.
81.stop: Stop when your back rounds or your knees touch down.
tips: Push the floor away with your hands so your upper back stays full, not sunk.
Keep your hips at the same height as your shoulders, not higher.
Spread your fingers wide and press your whole hand into the floor, not just the heel.

82.cue: Knees a hand's width off the floor, crawl forward and back. Count out loud.
how: Clear a path a few steps long, then kneel with hands under shoulders, toes tucked.
Lift your knees a hand's width off the floor, back flat and level.
Step one hand and the opposite foot forward together, then the other pair.
Take a few small steps forward, then crawl backwards the same way, breathing steadily.
Count out loud while the clock times the crawl, from your first step.
82.name: Bear crawl
82.setup: A clear path of a few steps on a floor that does not slip.
82.stop: Stop when your hips rise high or your knees touch down.
tips: Keep your steps short, a hand's length at most, so your hips stay still.
Keep your knees low, hovering just above the floor on every step.
Look at the floor a little ahead of your hands to keep your neck long.

83.cue: Forearm down, lift your hips, bottom leg hanging free. Count out loud.
how: Lie on your side on the floor beside a bed or sofa that stays put when you push it.
Put your top knee on its edge, elbow on the floor right under your shoulder.
Lift your hips into a straight line from knee to head, bottom leg hanging free.
Put your top hand on your hip and breathe slowly and steadily through the hold.
Count out loud; when this side ends, press Switch sides, then turn round.
83.name: Copenhagen side plank
83.setup: Top knee on the edge of a bed or sofa, forearm on the floor.
83.stop: Stop when your hips drop or your inner thigh hurts. Count the weaker side.
tips: Press your top knee down into the edge, since that is what lifts your hips.
Push the floor away with your forearm so your shoulder stays strong.
Keep your hips stacked and pressed forward, not tipping back.

84.cue: Hinge down, walk your hands out to a plank and back. Count out loud, breathe steadily.
how: Stand tall with a body length of clear floor in front of you, feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips and put your hands flat on the floor, bending your knees as needed.
Walk your hands out in small steps until your body is straight from heels to head.
Walk your hands back to your feet, then roll up slowly to stand tall.
